text: Dwoada no, abɔdeɛ mu nimdefoɔ a wɔfiri Stanford University School of Medicine de too dwa sɛ wɔayɛ nhwehwɛmu afidie foforɔ bi a ɛtumi kyɛ nkwammoa mu akuokuo: kyiipo ketewa pa ara bi a wotumi kunkyire gu krataa so a wobɛtumi de inkjet mfidie a yɛde kunkyire nneɛma ayɛ a koro biara boɔ bɛyɛ sɛ 1 U.S cent.
eng_text: On Monday, scientists from the Stanford University School of Medicine announced the invention of a new diagnostic tool that can sort cells by type: a tiny printable chip that can be manufactured using standard inkjet printers for possibly about one U.S. cent each.

text: Wɔn a wɔayɛ nhwehwɛmu akɔ nkan se yei bɛtumi ama yɛanhunu kokoram, nsamanwa, babaso werɛmfoɔ ne atiridii yareɛ ano ntɛm, wɔ ayarefoɔ a wɔwɔ aman a ɛntuu mpɔn mu, bea a yareɛ bi tesɛ nufoɔ mu kokoram yareɛ a ɛkum nnipa kɛse sɛ yɛde toto aman a wɔwɔ sika ho a.
eng_text: Lead researchers say this may bring early detection of cancer, tuberculosis, HIV and malaria to patients in low-income countries, where the survival rates for illnesses such as breast cancer can be half those of richer countries.

text: JAS 39C Gripen hwee ase wɔ wiemhyɛn kwantempɔn mu berɛ a na abɔ bɛyɛ anɔpa 9:30 (0230 UTC) maa ogya tɔɔ mu, ne saa nti wɔamma kwan amma wiemhyɛn biara ankɔ amanɔne.
eng_text: The JAS 39C Gripen crashed onto a runway at around 9:30 am local time (0230 UTC) and exploded, closing the airport to commercial flights.

text: Na wiemhyɛnkafoɔ no yɛ Squadron Leader Dilokrit Pattavee.
eng_text: The pilot was identified as Squadron Leader Dilokrit Pattavee.

text: Dawurubɔ dwuma a ɛwɔ kuro no mu de too dwa sɛ ogya atɔ lɔɔre a ɛdi dwuma wɔ wiemhyɛn gyinabea bi mu.
eng_text: Local media reports an airport fire vehicle rolled over while responding.

text: Vidal a na wadi mfeɛ 28 afiri Sevilla akɔ Barça mfeɛ mmiɛnsa mu nie.
eng_text: 28-year-old Vidal had joined Barça three seasons ago, from Sevilla.

text: Firi mmerɛ a Vidal baa Catalan ahenkuro no, wasi akan 49 ama bɔɔlobɔkuo no.
eng_text: Since moving to the Catalan-capital, Vidal had played 49 games for the club.

text: Ɔyɛkyerɛ no hyɛɛ aseɛ bɛyɛ 11:00 (UTC+1) wɔ Whitehall bea a ɛne Downing Street a apolisifoɔ hyɛn anim hɔ bɔ nhwɛanim no, saa beaeɛ yi na Mansoafoɔ panin te.
eng_text: The protest started around 11:00 local time (UTC+1) on Whitehall opposite the police-guarded entrance to Downing Street, the Prime Minister's official residence.

text: 11:00 bɔ paa ho ara no, nnipa a wɔreyɛ yɛkyerɛ too ban maa teaseɛnam biara antumi ankɔ wɔ Whitehall hɔ.
eng_text: Just after 11:00, protesters blocked traffic on the northbound carriage in Whitehall.

text: Ɛbɔɔ 11:20 kenn, apolisifoɔ no ka kyerɛɛ wɔn a wɔreyɛ yɛkyerɛ no wɔnkɔ bama no so, na wɔkyerɛ sɛ ɛwɔ sɛ wɔn yɛkyerɛ no fa kwan pa so na beaeɛ hɔ nso ammɔ kyenku.
eng_text: At 11:20, the police asked the protesters to move back on to the pavement, stating that they needed to balance the right to protest with the traffic building up.

text: Ɛbɔɔ bɛyɛ 11:29 no, na wɔn a wɔreyɛ yɛkyerɛ no nyinaa akɔ Whitehall, wɔatera Trafalgar Square, wɔ Strand kwan ho a wɔatu atene nam Aldwych na wɔnam Kingsway de rekɔ Holborn bea a Conservative Party reyɛ wɔn Spring Forum wɔ ahomegyebea a yɛfrɛ no Grand Connaught Rooms.
eng_text: Around 11:29, the protest moved up Whitehall, past Trafalgar Square, along the Strand, passing by Aldwych and up Kingsway towards Holborn where the Conservative Party were holding their Spring Forum in the Grand Connaught Rooms hotel.

text: Sԑ yԑde Nadal ne Canadani no toto ho wɔ mprԑ dodoɔ a obi adi ne yɔnko so nkonima, ԑyԑ 7-2.
eng_text: Nadal's head to head record against the Canadian is 7–2.

text: Nansa yi ara Raonic twaa no wɔ Brisbane akansie no mu.
eng_text: He recently lost against Raonic in the Brisbane Open.

text: Akansie no baa awieeԑ no, King of Clay kaa sԑ, "Ɛyԑ m’anigye sԑ masane aduru akansie a ԑho hia pa ara no awieeԑ. Mewɔ ha sԑ mԑyere me ho na magye."
eng_text: After the match, King of Clay said, "I am just excited about being back in the final rounds of the most important events. I am here to try to win this."

text: "Panama Papers" yԑ asԑm a yԑde gyina hɔ ma Panama mmara adwumakuo Mossack Fonseca, nkrataa bԑyԑ ɔpepem du a ԑfaa kwatikwan so kɔpuee nsԑntwerԑfoɔ hɔ wɔ 'spring' 2016 mu no.
eng_text: "Panama Papers" is an umbrella term for roughly ten million documents from Panamanian law firm Mossack Fonseca, leaked to the press in spring 2016.

text: Nkrataa no kyerԑԑ sԑ sikakorabea du-nnan bi boaa wɔn a wɔne wɔn yԑ adwuma a wɔwɔ sika pa ara no maa wɔde Amerika sika no ɔpepem sieeԑ sԑdeԑ ԑbԑyԑ a wɔntua ԑho toɔ ne ԑho sika biara.
eng_text: The documents showed fourteen banks helped wealthy clients hide billions of US dollars of wealth to avoid taxes and other regulations.

text: Britain dawurobɔ krataa Guardian no susuu ho sԑ, na Deutsche sikakorabea no wɔ tumi wɔ shell nnwumakuo 1200 a wɔde wɔn yԑԑ saa adeԑ no nkyekyԑmu mmiԑnsa mu baako so.
eng_text: British newspaper The Guardian suggested Deutsche Bank controlled roughly a third of the 1200 shell companies used to accomplish this.

text: Ɔyԑkyerԑ ahodoɔ kɔɔ so wɔ wiase nyinaa, wɔde nnipa bebree kɔgyinaa mmara ano de wɔn kɔguu afiase, ԑnna Iceland ne Pakistan aban mu mpanimfoɔ de wɔn akonnwa too hɔ.
eng_text: There were protests worldwide, several criminal prosecutions, and the leaders of the governments of Iceland and Pakistan both resigned.

text: Wɔwoo Ma wɔ Hong Kong, nanso ɔsuaa adeԑ wɔ New York University ne Harvard Law School ԑnna ԑduruu mmerԑ bi maa na ɔkuta Amerika krataa a "ԑma no kwan ma ɔtena hɔ daa" no bi.
eng_text: Born in Hong Kong, Ma studied at New York University and Harvard Law School and once held an American permanent resident "green card".

text: Hsieh kyerԑԑ wɔ abatoɔ berԑ no mu sԑ, ɔhaw bi ba a, Ma bԑdwane afiri ɔman no mu.
eng_text: Hsieh implied during the election that Ma might flee the country during a time of crisis.

text: Hsieh sane kaa sԑ Ma a ne ho yԑ fԑ wɔ mfonin mu no, adepa biara nni ne mu.
eng_text: Hsieh also argued that the photogenic Ma was more style than substance.

text: Nsԑm a wɔka faa ne ho nyinaa akyiri no, Ma dii nkonim berԑ a ɔkyerԑԑ sԑdeԑ ɔbԑsi ne China aka abom no ho.
eng_text: Despite these accusations, Ma won handily on a platform advocating closer ties with the Chinese mainland.

text: Ɛnnԑ agokansini mapa no ne Alex Ovechkin a ɔbɔ ma Washington Capitals.
eng_text: Today's Player of the Day is Alex Ovechkin of the Washington Capitals.

text: Ɔtoo ntena mmienu ԑnna ɔboaa obi maa ɔtoo atena mprԑ mmienu wɔ Washington 5-3 nkonimdie a wɔnyaa no wɔ Atlanta Thrashers so no mu.
eng_text: He had 2 goals and 2 assists in Washington's 5-3 win over the Atlanta Thrashers.

text: Ovechkin mmoa a ԑdi kan wɔ anadwo no mu no ne deԑ na wɔde redi nkonim a rookie Nicklas Backstrom hyԑeԑ no;
eng_text: Ovechkin's first assist of the night was on the game-winning goal by rookie Nicklas Backstrom;

text: atena a ԑtɔ so mmienu a ɔtoeԑ no na na ԑyԑ deԑ ԑtɔ so aduosia a wahyԑ no saa agokansie berԑ no mu, wei maa no bԑyԑԑ onipa a ɔdikan a wahyԑ aduosia anaa deԑ ԑboro saa ԑfiri 1995-96 a Jaromir Jagr ne Mario Lemieux mu biara duruu saa adeԑ no ho no.
eng_text: his second goal of the night was his 60th of the season, becoming the first player to score 60 or more goals in a season since 1995-96, when Jaromir Jagr and Mario Lemieux each reached that milestone.

text: Batten tɔɔ so 190 wɔ 2008 Amerika Asikafoɔ din a ԑpueeԑ no mu a na ɔwɔ agyapadeԑ ne sika ne boɔ som Amerika sika no ɔpepem $2.3 billion.
eng_text: Batten was ranked 190th on the 2008 400 Richest Americans list with an estimated fortune of $2.3 billion.

text: Ɔwiee sukuu wɔ College of Arts & Science a ԑwɔ Virginia Suapɔn no mu wɔ afe 1950 mu; na ɔboa sukuu no pa ara.
eng_text: He graduated from the College of Arts & Sciences of the University of Virginia in 1950 and was a significant donor to that institution.

text: Wɔ paa agya too Abu Ghraib afiase a ԑwɔ Iraq no mu berԑ a basabasaeԑ kɔɔ so hɔ wɔ.
eng_text: Iraq's Abu Ghraib prison has been set alight during a riot.

text: Afiase hɔ bԑyԑԑ beaeԑ a ԑnyԑ wɔ berԑ a wɔhunuu sԑ wɔyԑ nneduafoɔ no ayakayakadeԑ wɔ hɔ berԑ a Amerika asogyafoɔ bԑgyeeԑ no akyi.
eng_text: The jail became notorious after prisoner abuse was discovered there after US forces took over.

text: Piquet Jr. nyaa nkwanhyia wɔ ‘2008 Singapore Grand Prix’ no mu berԑ a ɔgyina faa Fernando Alonso, saa berԑ no na ɔyii ahobanbɔ kaa no pueeԑ.
eng_text: Piquet Jr. crashed in the 2008 Singapore Grand Prix just after an early pit stop for Fernando Alonso, bringing out the safety car.

text: Berԑ a kaa a wɔwɔ Alonso anim no kɔɔ ahobanbɔ kaa no ase sԑ wɔrekɔbu fango no, ɔkɔɔ anim kɔdii nkonim.
eng_text: As the cars ahead of Alonso went in for fuel under the safety car, he moved up the pack to take victory.

text: Wɔyii Piquet Jr. adi berɛ a wɔwiee ‘2009 Hungarian Grand Prix’ no.
eng_text: Piquet Jr. was sacked after the 2009 Hungarian Grand Prix.

text: 8:46 a.m. pԑpԑԑpԑ na kuro no mu nyinaa yԑԑ dinn, de rekyerԑ berԑ a wiemhyԑn a ԑdi kan no hwee deԑ wɔasoma sԑ ԑnkɔhwe mu no mu.
eng_text: At exactly 8:46 a.m. a hush fell across the city, marking the exact moment the first jet struck its target.

text: Wɔde nkanea mmienu ahwԑ soro anadwofa no mu.
eng_text: Two beams of light have been rigged up to point skywards overnight.

text: Wɔgu so resi mmorosan afoforɔ nnum wɔ beaeԑ hɔ a wɔde beaeԑ a wɔbԑfa hyԑn ne nkaebea ahyԑ mfimfini.
eng_text: Construction is ongoing for five new skyscrapers at the site, with a transportation center and memorial park in the middle.

text: PBS so dwumadie no wɔ Emmy abasobɔdeɛ bɛyɛ aduonu nan ne akyire, na mberɛ ɔmo yi kyerɛ no na yɛ tia sen Sesame Street ne Mister Rogers' Neighborhood.
eng_text: The PBS show has more than two-dozen Emmy awards, and its run is shorter only than Sesame Street and Mister Rogers' Neighborhood.

text: Na mfonini no mu biara wɔ dwumadie no so bɛgyina ho ama asɛntitire a ɛwɔ nwoma pɔtee n'ya booboo ho afa anansesɛm bebreebe ho.
eng_text: Each episode of the show would focus on a theme in a specific book and then explore that theme through multiple stories.

text: Na dwumadie no nso bɛyɛ abɔdinkyerɛ fa nwoma a mmofra nkɔ hwehwɛ sɛ ɔkɔ wɔn nwomakorabea.
eng_text: Each show would also provide recommendations for books that children should look for when they went to their library.

text: John Grant, a ɔfri WNED Buffalo (Fie tenabea Reading Rainbow) kaa sɛ "Reading Ranibow akyerɛ mmofra deɛ nti a akenkan ho hia,…odo a ɛwɔ akenkan mu- [mfonini no] hyɛ mmofra no nkuran sɛ womfa nwoma na ɔnkenka."
eng_text: John Grant, from WNED Buffalo (Reading Rainbow's home station) said "Reading Rainbow taught kids why to read,... the love of reading — [the show] encouraged kids to pick up a book and to read."

text: Ebinom, a John Grant ka ho, gyidi sɛ sika a ɛho ayɛ den ne sesa sibea a aba nyansapɛ nwomasua wɔ tɛlɛvihyen so agudi mu na ɛde nsɛm a edidi so yi ba awie yɛ no.
eng_text: It is believed by some, including John Grant, that both the funding crunch and a shift in the philosophy of educational television programming contributed to ending the series.

text: Ewiem adehunufoɔ se asoɔkye a ԑwɔ kwansini 645 (1040 km) wɔ Cape Verde atɔeԑ fa mu no ano bԑtumi abrԑ ase ansa na ahunahuna wɔn a wɔte bԑn hɔ no.
eng_text: The storm, situated about 645 miles (1040 km) west of the Cape Verde islands, is likely to dissipate before threatening any land areas, forecasters say.

text: Seisei Fred wɔ mframa a ɛbɔ kwansini 105 dɔnhwere baako biara (165 km/h) ԑnna ԑde n’ani akyerԑ atifi-atɔeeԑ fam.
eng_text: Fred currently has winds of 105 miles per hour (165 km/h) and is moving towards the northwest.

text: Fred ne mframa a ano yԑ den pa ara wɔanya wɔ anaafoɔ ԑne apueeԑ fam wɔ Atlantic no mu wɔ berԑ a wɔde ewiem mfonintwa hyԑԑ aseԑ no, ԑnna ԑsane nso yԑ mframa gyampantrudu a wɔanya wɔ 35°W apueeԑ fam a ԑtɔ so mmiԑnsa.
eng_text: Fred is the strongest tropical cyclone ever recorded so far south and east in the Atlantic since the advent of satellite imagery, and only the third major hurricane on record east of 35°W.

text: Ɛbɔ 24, 1759 mu no, Arthur Guinness de ne nsa ano agyinaeԑ hyԑԑ mfeԑ 9,000 ase de maa St James' Gate Brewery a ԑwɔ Dublin, Ireland.
eng_text: On September 24, 1759, Arthur Guinness signed a 9,000 year lease for the St James' Gate Brewery in Dublin, Ireland.

text: Mfeԑ 250 akyi no, na Guinness abԑyԑ wiase adwumakuo a ԑma euros ɔpepem 10 (US$14.7 billion) ne akyire afe biara.
eng_text: 250 years later, Guinness has grown to a global business that turns over 10 billion euros (US$14.7 billion) every year.

text: Jonny Reid a ɔka wɔn a wɔtwi kaa ma A1GP New Zealand kuo no ho no ayԑ abakɔsԑm nnԑ sԑ watwi kaa ntԑm pa ara so de afa ‘Auckland Harbour Bridge’ a adi mfeԑ 48 wɔ New Zealand no so wɔ berԑ a wanto mmara.
eng_text: Jonny Reid, co-driver for the A1GP New Zealand team, today made history by driving the fastest over the 48-year-old Auckland Harbour Bridge, New Zealand, legally.

text: Owura Reid de mmirika a na ԑboro 160km/h tumi twii ‘New Zealand's A1GP kaa’, Black Beauty no faa fasuo no so mprԑ nson.
eng_text: Mr Reid managed to drive the New Zealand's A1GP car, Black Beauty at speeds over 160km/h seven times over the bridge.

text: New Zealand apolisifoɔ no antumi amfa wɔn afidie a wɔde hwԑ mmirikatuo no anhwԑ mmirika a Owura Reid retu ԑnam wɔ a Black Beauty wɔ fam no, berԑ a wɔtumi nyaa no no, na Owura Reid de ne mmirika no aba 160km/h.
eng_text: The New Zealand police had trouble using their speed radar guns to see how fast Mr Reid was going because of how low Black Beauty is, and the only time the police managed to clock Mr Reid was when he slowed down to 160km/h.

text: Abosome mmiԑnsa a atwam no mu no, wɔn a wɔakye wɔn bԑboro 80 na wɔagyae wɔn afiri ‘Central Booking facility’ hɔ wɔ berԑ a wɔammɔ wɔn kwaadu biara.
eng_text: In the last 3 months, over 80 arrestees were released from the Central Booking facility without being formally charged.

text: Oforisuo bosome no mu wɔ afe yi mu na ɔtԑmmuafoɔ Glynn de ɔhyԑ krataa maa beaeԑ no sԑ wɔnnyae wɔn a wɔakye wɔn ama aboro dɔnhwere aduonu-nnan firi berԑ a wɔkyee wɔn na kɔɔto antena wɔn asԑm no so no.
eng_text: In April this year, a temporary restaining order was issued by Judge Glynn against the facility to enforce the release of those held more than 24 hours after their intake who did not receive a hearing by a court commissioner.

text: ‘Commissioner’ no na ԑkyerԑ efiekɔ ho nhyehyԑeԑ a wɔde ma, sane yԑ kwaadu a polisini a ɔkyeeԑ no de bɔ ho adwuma. Afei ɔbɔ kwaadu no gu ɔman no kɔmpuita nhyehyԑeԑ no so ma wɔde wɔn ani di akyire.
eng_text: The commissioner sets bail, if granted, and formalizes the charges filed by the arresting officer. The charges are then entered into the state's computer system where the case is tracked.

text: Ɛda a wɔbԑfrԑ asԑm no nso yԑ da a ԑwɔ hɔ ma deԑ wɔabɔ no kwaadu no sԑ wɔbԑdi n’asԑm no ntԑntԑm.
eng_text: The hearing also marks the date for the suspect’s right to a speedy trial.

text: Peter Costello, deԑ ɔhwԑ Australian sikasԑm so na ɔsane nso yԑ obi a ‘Mansoafoɔ Panin John Howard’ nni hɔ a, ɔbԑdi ‘Liberal party’ no anim sԑ kandini no ataa ‘nuclear power industry’ wɔ Australia no akyi.
eng_text: Peter Costello, Australian treasurer and the man most likely to succeed Prime Minister John Howard as Liberal party leader has thrown his support behind a nuclear power industry in Australia.

text: Owura Costello se, sԑ kwan a wɔbԑfa so anya ‘nuclear power’ no yԑ deԑ wɔn ho bԑso a, Australia nhwԑ sԑ wɔbԑdi akyire na wɔde adi dwuma.
eng_text: Mr Costello said that when nuclear power generation becomes economically viable, Australia should pursue its use.

text: Owura Costello se,"sԑ ԑbԑyԑ deԑ obiara tumi tɔ bi a, yԑnnya bi. ԑne sԑ, mmara biara nni hɔ a ԑsi nuclear energy no ano".
eng_text: "If it becomes commercial, we should have it. That is, there's no in-principle objection to nuclear energy" Mr Costello said.

text: Sԑdeԑ Ansa de too dwa no, "na apolisifoɔ suro nneԑma bi a na wɔsusu sԑ ԑbԑtumi de ko a ԑtoɔ ntwa da bԑba no ho.
eng_text: According to Ansa, "police were concerned by a couple of top-level hits they feared might spark a full-blown war of succession.

text: Apolisifoɔ kyerԑ sԑ Lo Piccolo wɔ soro ԑfiri sԑ wabԑne Provenzano pԑn wɔ Palermo ԑnna ne suahunu kԑseԑ a ɔwɔ no nso ama wanya mpanimfoɔ no dɔ wɔ berԑ a wɔdi Provenzano nhyehyԑeԑ so sԑ wɔbԑwɔ fam sԑdeԑ ani mma wɔn ho na wɔahyԑ wɔntumi no mu kena.
eng_text: Police said Lo Piccolo had the upper hand because he had been Provenzano's right-hand man in Palermo and his greater experience won him the respect of the older generation of bosses as they pursued Provenzano's policy of keeping as low as possible while strengthening their power network.

text: Saa mpanimfoɔ yi yԑ wɔn a wɔbԑnee Provenzano wɔ berԑ a ɔmaa ‘Riina-driven’ ko a na wɔne ɔman no ko a ԑmaa Mafia nkurɔfoɔ, Giovanni Falcone ԑne Paolo Borsellino wui wɔ afe 1992 mu no to twaeԑ."
eng_text: These bosses had been reined in by Provenzano when he put an end to the Riina-driven war against the state that claimed the lives of Mafia crusaders Giovanni Falcone and Paolo Borsellino in 1992."

text: ‘Apple baanodani’ Steve Jobs nante kɔɔ soro hɔ ԑnna ɔyii iPhone no firii ne botom de daa fon no adi.
eng_text: Apple CEO Steve Jobs unveiled the device by walking onto the stage and taking the iPhone out of his jeans pocket.

text: Berԑ a ɔrekasa wɔ ne dɔnhwere mmienu kasakyerԑ no mu no, ɔkaa sԑ, "Ɛnnԑ Apple resane ayԑ fon bio, Yԑrebԑyԑ abakɔsԑm ԑnnԑ".
eng_text: During his 2 hour speech he stated that "Today Apple is going to reinvent the phone, We are going to make history today".

text: Brazil yɛ Roman Catholicfoↄ man a ɛso paa wↄ asase yi so, na Roman Cathloic Asↄre no akasa atia bobeasu baako awareɛ a wↄde bɛhyɛ mmara aseɛ wↄ ↄman no mu mpɛn pii.
eng_text: Brazil is the largest Roman Catholic country on Earth, and the Roman Catholic Church has consistently opposed the legalization of same-sex marriage in the country.

text: Mfeɛ 10 nie a Brazil Mmarahyɛ Abadwafoↄ abooboo gye a wↄbɛgye atom no ho, na seesei deɛ Rio Grande do Sul nko ara na wagye saa mmara kwan so awareɛ yi atom.
eng_text: The National Congress of Brazil has debated legalization for 10 years, and such civil marriages are currently only legal in Rio Grande do Sul.

text: Marta Suplicy, Sao Poalo "mayor" a w'atwam no na ↄtwerɛɛ mmara a edi kan no. Saa mmara yi a wↄde too dwa no akodi Roberto Jefferson nsam, berɛ a wↄyɛɛ ɛho nsakraeɛ wieɛ no.
eng_text: The original bill was drafted by former mayor of São Paulo, Marta Suplicy. The proposed legislation, after being amended, is now in the hands of Roberto Jefferson.

text: Ayɛkyerɛfoↄ yi anidasoↄ ne sɛ ɛdom ↄpepem 1.2 de wↄn nsa bɛhyɛ nwoma no aseɛ na wↄde akↄdan Mmarahyɛ Abadwafoↄ no wↄ Abubuo mu.
eng_text: Protesters hope to collect a petition of 1.2 million signatures to present to the National Congress in November.

text: Akyiri yi a ɛbɛdaa adi sɛ mmusua dodoↄ no ara rehwehwɛ mmara kwan so mmoa de ako atia tu a wↄpɛ sɛ wotu wↄn no, wↄyɛɛ nhyiamu bi wↄ Mpↄtam Mmarahyɛbeae wↄ East Bay Ɔbɛnem da ɛtↄ so 20 maa wↄn a woabu wↄn wↄ adansie nsɛmsɛm mu no.
eng_text: After it became apparent that many families were seeking legal help to fight the evictions, a meeting was held on March 20 at the East Bay Community Law Center for the victims of the housing scam.

text: Berɛ a wↄn a wↄhan dan no firi aseɛ kaa deɛ ɛtoo wↄn no, mmusua ahodoↄ a wↄn ho wↄ asɛm yi mu no behunu prɛko pɛ sɛ OHA odwumayeni baako Carolyn Wilson awia sika a wↄde too dan no ase no na wadwane afiri kuro no mu.
eng_text: When the tenants started sharing what had occurred to them, most of the families involved suddenly realized that Carolyn Wilson of the OHA had stolen their security deposits, and skipped out of town.

text: Wↄn a wↄhan dan wↄ Lockwood Gardens no gye di sɛ wobetu mmusua afoforↄ bɛyɛ 40 anaa deɛ ɛboro saa, efiri berɛ a wonyaa no nteeɛ sɛ OHA apolisifoↄ reyɛ nhwehwɛmu afa aban adansie nwumakuo afoforↄ ho wↄ Oakland a wↄn nso ho wↄ adansie bukata nsɛmsɛm yi mu no.
eng_text: Tenants at Lockwood Gardens believe that there may be another 40 families or more to face eviction, since they learned that OHA police are also investigating other public housing properties in Oakland that may be caught up in the housing scam.

text: Agofomma no twaa "Maui's War Memorial" agropramma dwumadie no mu, a na nnipa 9000 na ɛsɛ ɛba, na wↄde kyɛwpa ↄmaa wↄn akyidifoↄ.
eng_text: The band canceled the show at Maui's War Memorial Stadium, which was set to be attended by 9,000 people, and apologized to fans.

text: Adwumakuo a ɛhwɛ agofomma no so, HK Management Inc., anka deɛ nti a wotwaa mo berɛ a edi kan wↄ september 20, nanso da edi hↄ no wↄde hyɛɛ ɛho nhyehyeɛ a ankↄ yie.
eng_text: The band's management company, HK Management Inc., gave no initial reason when they canceled on September 20, but blamed logistical reasons by the next day.

text: Wↄde Greekfoↄ alↄyafoↄ a ↄmo agye din, Sakis Kechagioglou ne George Nikolakopoulos atom wↄ Athens efiase wↄ korydallus, ɛsaine sɛ wodi korↄno ne kɛtɛasehyɛ ho fↄ.
eng_text: The famous Greek lawyers, Sakis Kechagioglou and George Nikolakopoulos have been imprisoned in the Athens' jail of Korydallus, as they were found guilty of graft and corruption.

text: Yei ama asɛm kɛseɛ asↄre wↄ Greekfoↄ mmaranimfoↄ kuo no mu esiane nneɛma a ɛmfa mmara kwan so a atenmufoↄ ne alↄyafoↄ ahodoↄ no de wↄn ho hyɛɛ mu mfeɛ a atwam a abɛda adie.
eng_text: As a result of this, a big scandal within the Greek legal community has been raised through the exposure of illegal actions that judges, lawyers, solicitors and attorneys have done during the previous years.

text: Berɛ a nsɛntwerɛni Makis Triantafylopoulos daa nsɛm bi adi wↄ ne tɛlɛbihyɛn so dwumadie a agye din "Zoungla" wↄ Alpha TV so nnawↄtwe kakra a etwam no, wotuu mmarahyɛ badwani ne lↄyani Petros Mantouvalos adeɛ so efiri sɛ na wↄn a ↄne wↄn yɛ adwuma no de wↄn ho ahyehyɛ korↄno ne keteasehye mu.
eng_text: A few weeks ago, after the information published by the journalist Makis Triantafylopoulos in his popular Television show "Zoungla" in Alpha TV, the member of Parliament and lawyer, Petros Mantouvalos was abdicated as members of his office had been involved in illegal graft and corruption.

text: Afei nso, wakye otɛmmuafoↄ kunini Evangelos Kalousis ato efiase efiri sɛ na odi fↄ wↄ kɛtɛasehyɛ ne ↄbrabↄne ho.
eng_text: Moreover, top judge Evangelos Kalousis is imprisoned as he found guilty of corruption and degenerate behaviour.

text: Roberts poeɛ koraa sɛ ↄbɛka berɛ a ↄgye di sɛ nkwa hyɛɛ aseɛ, asemmisa a eho hia paa berɛ a yɛresusuw nyinsen a wotu gu ho nnyinasosɛm no, na ↄkaeɛ sɛ ɛnyɛ papa sɛ ↄbɛka nsɛm pↄtee a ɛte saa ho asɛm.
eng_text: Roberts flatly refused to say about when he believes life begins, an important question when considering the ethics of abortion, saying that it would be unethical to comment on the specifics of likely cases.

text: Nanso, ↄsan tii asɛm a waka dada sɛ Roe v. Wade yɛ "mmara a woagye atom wↄ ↄman no mu", de sii hia a ehia sɛ asennibea kunini no gyinae a wosi no betoatoa so no so dua.
eng_text: He did, however, reiterate his earlier statement that Roe v. Wade was the "settled law of the land", emphasizing the importance of consistent Supreme Court rulings.

text: Ↄsan ka sii so sɛ ↄgye hokwan a obi wↄ sɛ ↄyɛ deɛ ↄpɛ a obi mfeefee ne nsɛm mu a Roe gyinaa so de sii gyinae no di.
eng_text: He also confirmed that he believed in the implied right to privacy which the Roe decision depended upon.

text: Maroochydore dii kan wↄ pon no so, na ↄde mma nsia na edii Noosa a ↄtↄↄ so mmienu no anim.
eng_text: Maroochydore had finished on top of the ladder, six points clear of Noosa in second.

text: Afa mmienu yi hyiaa wↄ ↄfa a edi faenal no anim a ɛyɛ titire paa na ɛhↄ na Noosa de mma 11 twaa wↄn a wodii nkonim no ho.
eng_text: The two sides would meet in the major semi final where Noosa ran out winners by 11 points.

text: Afei Maroochydore dii Caboolture so nkonim wↄ faenal a edi kan no mu.
eng_text: Maroochydore then defeated Caboolture in the Preliminary Final.

text: Hesperonychus elizabethae fri Dromaeosauridae abusua no mu na Velociraptor yɛ ne nua.
eng_text: Hesperonychus elizabethae is a species of the family Dromaeosauridae and is a cousin of Velociraptor .

text: Wↄgye di sɛ saa anomaa yi a ne ho wↄ nhwi, ne mogya mu yɛ hye na ↄwe mmoa afoforo nam yi nantewee ne nan mmienu so ntenten mu a na ne bↄwerɛ te sɛ Velociraptor deɛ no.
eng_text: This fully feathered, warm blooded bird of prey was believed to have walked upright on two legs with claws like the Velociraptor.

text: Esiane sɛ ne bↄwerɛ a ɛtↄ so mmienu no yɛ keseɛ nti, wↄtoo no din Hesperonychus a asekyerɛ ne "bↄwerɛ a ɛkyerɛ epuei."
eng_text: Its second claw was larger, giving rise to the name Hesperonychus which means "western claw."

text: Sɛ yɛde nsukyene a ebubu no to nkyɛn a, ewim tebea a ano yɛ den no mmoa nhyehyeɛ a wↄreyɛ de aboa no.
eng_text: In addition to the crushing ice, extreme weather conditions have been hampering rescue efforts.

text: Pitman kaeɛ sɛ nneɛma rensesa kosi nnawↄtwe a edi hↄ no mu baabi.
eng_text: Pittman suggested that conditions wouldn't improve until sometime next week.

text: Sɛdeɛ Pitmann kyerɛ no, nsukyene no dodoↄ ne emu duro no yɛ deɛ ɛnyɛ koraa, a ato wↄn a wↄkye sukraman no wↄ mfeɛ 15 a etwam yi mu.
eng_text: The amount and thickness of the pack ice, according to Pittman, is the worst it has been for sealers in the past 15 years.

text: Dawubo ntrɛmu wɔ Red Lake mpɔtam nnɛ sɛ ayie ma Jeff Weise ne nnipa nkron no mu mmiɛnsa a wɔyɛ wɔn ayayade hyɛɛ sɛɛ wa akyeree sukuuni foforo ɛfa etuo tutuɔ a ɛkɔ so wɔ sukuu mu ho wɔ ɔbɛnem da ɛtɔso aduonu baako.
eng_text: News spread in the Red Lake community today as funerals for Jeff Weise and three of the nine victims were held that another student was arrested in connection with the school shootings of March 21.

text: Tumikurafoɔ kaa biribi ketewa wɔ mmara kwan so a antra ɔkyeree a ɔkɔɔ so nnɛ no ho.
eng_text: Authorities said little officially beyond confirming today's arrest.

text: Nanso, obi a ɔwɔ nhweheɛmu no ho nimdeɛ kakyerɛɛ Minneaspolis Star-Tribune sɛ ɛyɛ Louis Jourdain, Guamutenanyi Ntɔn Red Lake Floyed Jourdain ba barima a woadi mfeɛ dunsia no.
eng_text: However, a source with knowledge of the investigation told the Minneapolis Star-Tribune that it was Louis Jourdain, 16-year old son of Red Lake Tribal Chairman Floyd Jourdain.

text: Yɛnnim soboɔ ko a wɔbɛbɔ wɔ saa bere yi mu anaa deɛ ɛmaa tumikurafoɔ kɔɔ aberanteɛ no hɔ nanso dumadie no nhyehyɛyɛ ahyɛaseɛ wɔ aban asɛnnibea.
eng_text: It is not known at this time what charges will be laid or what led authorities to the boy but juvenile proceedings have begun in federal court.

text: Lodin san ka kaa ho sɛ wↄn a wodi anim no sii gyinae sɛ wobetwa aba a wↄbɛto no ne mprenu suo no mu de abↄ Afganistanfoↄ sikasɛm ne ahobammↄ nsɛm a abatoↄ foforo de ba no ho ban.
eng_text: Lodin also said officials decided to cancel the runoff in order to save Afghans the expense and security risk of another election.

text: Aman foforↄ ananmusifoↄ a wↄwↄ ho no anhu biribi pↄtee wↄ Afganistan mmara no mu a ɛma eho hia sɛ wↄto aba no ne mprenu soↄ.
eng_text: Diplomats said that they had found enough ambiguity in the Afghan constitution to determine the runoff as unnecessary.

text: Yei ne amanneɛbↄ a ɛka sɛ sɛ wotwa aba a wↄbeto no ne mprenu soↄ no mu a, na watia mmara no bↄ abira.
eng_text: This contradicts earlier reports, which said that cancelling the runoff would have been against the constitution.

text: Na wiemhyen no ani kyerɛ Irkutsk na na asraafoↄ na na wↄreka.
eng_text: The aircraft had been headed to Irkutsk and was being operated by interior troops.

text: Wↄyɛɛ nhwehwɛmu ho nhyehyeɛ.
eng_text: An inquiry was established to investigate.

text: Il-76 edi dwuma titire wↄ Russia ne Soviet asraafoↄ mu firi 1970 mfeɛ no mu reba no, na woanya akwanhyia a ɛyɛ hu wↄ Russia bosome a etwaam no.
eng_text: The Il-76 has been a major component of both the Russian and Soviet military since the 1970s, and had already seen a serious accident in Russia last month.

text: Wↄ Ahinime da etↄ so 7 no afiri no fa bi ho baa asɛm berɛ a etui no, nanso obiara empira. Russia sii Il-76 kwan sɛ onntu mmerɛ tiawa bi mu wↄ saa akwanhyia no akyi no.
eng_text: On October 7 an engine separated on takeoff, without injuries. Russia briefly grounded Il-76s after that accident.

text: Wↄtoo Trans-Alaska Pipeline System a ne tenten yɛ akwansin 800 no mu berɛ a ankorɛ mpempem pii a na fango wom bu faa so wↄ Fairbanks anafoↄ fam, Alaska no.
eng_text: 800 miles of the Trans-Alaska Pipeline System were closed down following a spill of thousands of barrels of crude oil south of Fairbanks, Alaska.

text: Berɛ a wↄreso nhyehye a wↄayɛ de si ogya ano no ahwɛ no, akanea dumdumee na ɛmaa nsuaano no bue na fango no bu faa so wo beaeɛ a ɛbɛn Fort Greely pump station 9.
eng_text: A power failure following a routine fire-command system test caused relief valves to open and crude oil overflowed near the Fort Greely pump station 9.

text: Nsuaano a ebueɛ no hyɛɛ mfiri no so na ɛmaa fango no faa adeɛ trɛtrɛ bi so koguu akorade a etumi fa ankorɛ 55,000 (galↄn ↄpepem 2.3).
eng_text: The valves opening allowed a pressure release for the system and oil flowed on a pad to a tank that can hold 55,000 barrels (2.3 million gallons).

text: Ebeduu wukuada awia no, na ankorɛ no fa a ɛkwan da no gu so nwunu esaine hyew a ɛbɛyɛ sɛ agyina mu no.
eng_text: As of Wednesday afternoon, the tank vents were still leaking probably from thermal expansion inside the tank.

text: Beaeɛ foforↄ a wↄkora nneɛma a ɛwↄ akoradeɛ no ase a ebetumi afa ankorɛ 104,500 no nya nyɛɛ ma.
eng_text: Another secondary containment area below the tanks capable of holding 104,500 barrels was not yet filled to capacity.

text: Asɛm a ↄkaeɛ wↄ tɛlɛbihyɛn dwumadie a na ɛrekↄ so no yɛ berɛ a edi kan a Iran mpaninfo agye atom sɛ anohyetoↄ no anya nsunsuansoↄ bi wↄ wↄn so.
eng_text: The comments, live on television, were the first time that senior Iranian sources have admitted that the sanctions are having any effect.

text: Ebi ne sikasɛm ho anohyetoↄ ne bra a European Union abra fango a wↄde firi hↄ kↄ aman hodoↄ so kↄtↄn no, a ɛde mfasoↄ a wonya firi aman hodoↄ so ↄha mu nhyehyɛmu 80 na ɛba Iran man no mu.
eng_text: They include financial restrictions and a ban by the European Union on the export of crude oil, from which the Iranian economy receives 80% of its foreign income.

text: Wↄ bosome amanneɛbↄ a nkyeɛ koraa mu no, OPEC kaeɛ sɛ fango no dodoↄ so ate aba fam koraa wɛ mfeɛ aduonu mu nie opepem 2.8 ankorɛ da biara.
eng_text: In its most recent monthly report, OPEC said exports of crude had fallen to their lowest level for two decades at 2.8 million barrels per day.

text: Ↄman no kannifoↄ kunini, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, aka sɛ wↄn ho a wↄde to fango so no "sum afiri" a efiri berɛ a Islamfoↄ a wↄwↄ Iran no de nhyɛ sesaa aban no mu wo 1979 na ɛno na ɛsɛ sɛ ↄman no gye ne ho firi mu.
eng_text: The country's supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, has described the dependency on oil as "a trap" dating from before Iran's Islamic revolution in 1979 and from which the country should free itself.

text: Sɛ afiri no reba asase so na edu wiem, bɛyɛ 5am (eastern time) a, wↄhwɛ kwan sɛ ɛbɛyɛ yɛkyerɛ kakra bi ma wↄn a wↄwↄ Northern California, Oregon, Nevada ne Utah.
eng_text: When the capsule gets to Earth and enters the atmosphere, at about 5am (eastern time), it is expected to put on quite a light show for folks in Northern California, Oregon, Nevada, and Utah.

text: Wbehu afiri no te sɛ nsoromma a etu nam wiem.
eng_text: The capsule will look much like a shooting star going across the sky.

text: Afiri no betu kwan a ne tenten bɛyɛ kilomita 12.8 anaa akwansini 8 anibu bi ara mu, a ebetumi efiri San Francisco akoduru Los Angeles wↄ sima baako mu ntɛm so.
eng_text: The capsule will be traveling at about 12.8 km or 8 miles per second, fast enough to go from San Francisco to Los Angeles in one minute.

text: Stardust bɛyɛ twerɛtohↄ foforↄ a obiara nyeɛ da sɛ afiri a ako wiem a asan aba asaase so ntɛm so, na ɛno beyi twerɛtohↄ a ɛda hↄ wↄ Kotonimma afe 1969 berɛ a Apolo X afiri no san baeɛ no.
eng_text: Stardust will set a new all-time record for being the fastest spacecraft to return to Earth, breaking the previous record set in May of 1969 during the return of the Apollo X command module.

text: Tom Duxbury, Stardust dwumadie no sohwɛfoↄ kaeɛ sɛ “ɛbefa Northen California atↄɛ fam beaeɛ a ɛbɛn ɛpo no na ɛbɛma wiem ahyerɛn firi California de kↄ central Oregon na akↄ fa Nevada ne Idaho na ewura Utah.”
eng_text: “It will move over the west coast of northern California and will light the sky from California through central Oregon and on through Nevada and Idaho and into Utah,” Tom Duxbury, Stardust's project manager said.

text: Owura Rudd gyinaeɛ a w'asi sɛ ↄde ne nsa bɛhyɛ Kyoto ewiem nsakraeɛ apam no ase no ayi United States asi nkyɛn, na ↄno nkoaa abɛyɛ ↄman a woanya nkoanim a ↄmfaa ne nsa nhyɛɛ apam no ase.
eng_text: Mr. Rudd's decision to sign the Kyoto climate accord isolates the United States, which will now be the only developed nation not to ratify the agreement.

text: Australia Conservative aban a etwam no ampene so sɛ ↄde ne nsa bɛhyɛ Kyoto aseɛ, na okae sɛ ɛbesɛe ↄman no sikasɛm esaine sɛ wↄde wↄn ho ato fagudeɛ a wodi ho dwa wↄ aman foforↄ so paa, na mframa bↄne a epue firi mfiri mu mmara no nkyekyere aman be te sɛ India ne China.
eng_text: Australia's former conservative government refused to ratify Kyoto, saying it would damage the economy with its heavy reliance on coal exports, while countries like India and China were not bound by emissions targets.

text: Wↄ eBay abakↄsɛm mu no, yei ne agyapadeɛ kɛseɛ a woatumi atↄ.
eng_text: It is the biggest acquisition in eBay's history.

text: Adwumakuo no hwɛ kwan sɛ wobenya mfasoↄ afiri mmeaeɛ ahodoↄ na woagye din wↄ mmeaeɛ a Skype agye ntini, te sɛ China, Europe atↄeɛ fam, ne Brazil.
eng_text: The company hopes to diversify its profit sources and gain popularity in areas where Skype holds a strong position, such as China, Eastern Europe, and Brazil.

text: Abodeɛ mu nyasahunufoↄ susu sɛ Enceladus keka ne ho na nkwa wom na ɛbɛyɛ sɛ Saturn nya ne "icy E ring" firi mu.
eng_text: Scientists have suspected Enceladus as geologically active and a possible source of Saturn's icy E ring.

text: Enceladus tumi dan adeɛ ani sene biribiara wↄ okyinnsoromma kuo no mu, etumi dan owia hann a ɛka no ani bɛyɛ ↄha mu nkyekyemu 90.
eng_text: Enceladus is the most reflective object in the solar system, reflecting about 90 percent of the sunlight that hits it.

text: Adwumakuo a wↄyɛ kↄmputa so agodie Konami aka wↄ Japanfoↄ kowaa krataa ɛnnɛ sɛ wonya nda agodie a woato din Six Days in Fallujah no adi.
eng_text: The game publisher Konami stated today in a Japanese newspaper that they will not be releasing the game Six Days in Fallujah.

text: Agodie yi gyina Second Battle of Fallujah, ntↄkwa a ano yɛ den a ɛda Americafoↄ ne Iraqfoↄ asraafoↄ no ntam.
eng_text: The game is based on the Second Battle of Fallujah, a vicious battle between American and Iraqi forces.

text: ACMA san hunui sɛ ɛmfa ho sɛ na wↄreyi sini no wↄ internɛt so no, Big Brother anto sini a wↄde to internɛt so no ho mmara no, efiri sɛ na wonkoraa sini no wↄ Big Brother wɛbsaet no so.
eng_text: The ACMA also found that despite the video being streamed on the Internet, Big Brother had not breached online content censorship laws as the media had not been stored on Big Brother's website.

text: Dawurubo adwuma ho mmara (Broadcasting Services Act) boa ma wↄtoto nneɛma a wↄde gu internɛt so no yiye, nanso ɛsɛ sɛ wↄkora nneɛma no wↄ kↄmputa no so na ama woatumi abu no sɛ Internɛt so adeɛ.
eng_text: The Broadcasting Services Act provides for the regulation of Internet content, however to be considered Internet content, it must physically reside on a server.

text: United States ananmusini asoeɛ a ɛwɔ Nairobi a ɛwɔ Kenya man mu de kɔkɔbɔ ato dwa sɛ "atuturafoɔ a wɔfiri Somalia" refa adwene sɛ wɔbɛ to topaeɛ wɔ Kenya ne Ethiopia.
eng_text: The United States embassy located in Nairobi, Kenya has issued a warning that "extremists from Somalia" are planning to launch suicide bomb attacks in Kenya and Ethiopia.

text: U.S se wɔanya no nteeɛ afiri nnipakuo bi a wɔamfa wɔn din anto dwa hɔ sɛ wɔde topae bɛhyɛ nnipa bi ho de akɔsɛe "mmea atitire" a ɛwɔ Ethiopia ne Kenya man mu.
eng_text: The U.S. says it has received information from an undisclosed source that specifically mentions the use of suicide bombers to will blow up "prominent landmarks" in Ethiopia and Kenya.

text: Mmere tenten bi a atwam ansa wɔrebɛyɛ "The Daily Show" ne "The Cobert report" dwumadie no na Heck ne Johnson nyaa anisoadehunu bi sɛ wɔbɛdi dwuma bi tesɛ nsɛntwerɛ dwuma – ne kaseɛbɔ - berɛ a na wɔda so yɛ adesuafoɔ wɔ UW wɔ afe 1988 mu.
eng_text: Long before The Daily Show and The Colbert Report, Heck and Johnson envisioned a publication that would parody the news—and news reporting—when they were students at UW in 1988.

text: Ɛfiri mmerɛ a "The Onion" hyɛ wɔn dwumadie ase, wɔabɛyɛ nsɛntwerɛkuo anokwafoɔ a yԑagye wɔn adi yie a wɔatintim nsɛm no bi wɔ krataa so, wɔsane nso wɔ wԑbsaite a nnipa 5,000,000 kɔɔ so kɔkenkann Ahinime bosome no mu, wɔbɔ nnoɔma ho dawuro na afei nso wɔde nsɛm to dwa nnɔnhwere 24 da mu no nyinaa, foforɔ a wɔde abɛka ho nso ne asase ho mfonin a ɛfa wiase ho nyinaa a ne din de "Our Dumb World".
eng_text: Since its inception, The Onion has become a veritable news parody empire, with a print edition, a website that drew 5,000,000 unique visitors in the month of October, personal ads, a 24 hour news network, podcasts, and a recently launched world atlas called Our Dumb World.

text: Al Gore ԑne General Tommy Franks amma dawura mu nsԑntitire no ahaw wɔn (Na Gore wɔ hɔ na ‘The Onion’ de too dwa sԑ ɔne Tipper regye wɔn ani wɔ nna mu berԑ a ɔdii nkoguo wɔ ‘Abatoɔ Mpasua’ 2000 so no) no akyi.
eng_text: Al Gore and General Tommy Franks casually rattle off their favorite headlines (Gore's was when The Onion reported he and Tipper were having the best sex of their lives after his 2000 Electoral College defeat).

text: Wɔn atwerɛfoɔ no mu pii akɔso anya nsusuansoɔ kɛse wɔ Jon Stewart ne Stephen Colbert nsɛm ho amaneɛbo dwumadie no so.
eng_text: Many of their writers have gone on to wield great influence on Jon Stewart and Stephen Colbert's news parody shows.

text: Mfonin ho dwumadie nso ka nkaebɔ a Bucharest City Hall de agu akwan mu sɛ wɔde bɛsan apaw Romania kuropɔn ho ntoma sɛ wɔyɛ adeɛ yie wɔ abɔdeɛ ne nnoɔma fɛɛfɛ ho.
eng_text: The artistic event is also part of a campaign by the Bucharest City Hall that seeks to relaunch the image of the Romanian capital as a creative and colourful metropolis.

text: Kuro kɛseɛ no bɛyɛ kuro a ɛdi kan wɔ Europe anaafo apueeԑ fam a wɔbɛyɛ CowParade, ɛbɛyɛ mfonin dwumadie kɛse a ɛyɛ fɛ sen biribiara a ɛfiri Ayɛwohomumɔ bosome mu de kɔsi a Ɔsanaa afe yi.
eng_text: The city will be the first in southeastern Europe to host CowParade, the world's largest public art event, between June and August this year.

text: Nkaebɔ a wɔde too dwa ɛnnɛ no nso trɛ aban nhyehyɛeԑ a wɔde guu akwan mu Ɔbɛnem bosome no mu wɔ afe yi mu sɛ wɔbɛfa nnoɔma foforɔ ho ka.
eng_text: Today's announcement also extended the government's commitment made in March of this year to fund extra carriages.

text: Ahaasa bɛka ho ma no yɛ apem ne ahaasa sɛnea ɛbɛboa ama obiara ho bɛhenhaa no.
eng_text: An additional 300 brings the total to 1,300 carriages to be acquired to relieve overcrowding.

text: Christopher Garcia a ɔyɛ ɔkasamafoɔ ma Los Angeles Apolisifoɔ kaa sɛ aberanteɛ no a wɔakye no no, nhwehwɛmu a wɔreyɛ fa ne ho ne sɛ watra n’ahyeɛ na mmom ɛnyɛ nsɛmbɔne a ɔdiiɛ no.
eng_text: Christopher Garcia, a spokesperson of the Los Angeles Police Department, said the suspected male offender is being investigated for trespassing rather than vandalism.

text: Ahyɛnsodeɛ no ansee anisoɔ; wɔde tarpdi tuntum na ɛsiesie, ɛnna wɔde asomdwoeɛ ne akoka ahyɛnsodeɛ asi "O" ananmu sɛnea wɔbɛ kan no sɛ atwerɛdeɛ ketewa "e".
eng_text: The sign was not physically damaged; the modification was done using black tarpaulins decorated with signs of peace and heart to alter the "O" to read lowercase "e".

text: Deԑ ԑde ‘Red tide’ ba ne ‘Karenia brevis’, aboa a ɔwɔ nkwaboa baako pԑ a ԑno ara ba no mmorosoɔ a ԑkyԑne deԑ ԑsԑ sԑ anka ԑyԑ no.
eng_text: Red tide is caused by a higher than normal concentration of Karenia brevis, a naturally-occurring single-celled marine organism.

text: Abɔdeɛ mu nneɛma betumi aka abom ma tebea no ayɛ paa ara na aboa ma saa mmoawa yi adɔɔso ntɛmtɛm yie.

text: Ɛwom sɛ na ɔyɛ ‘Olympic ne World champion’ deɛ, na Saito sane yɛ All Japan Judo Federation mu ekuo panin ansa na ɔrewu.
eng_text: As well as a former Olympic and World champion, Saito was the All Japan Judo Federation training committee chairman at the time of his death.

text: Nnipa a wɔkɔɔ apontoɔ no ase bɛyɛ 100, wɔkɔɔ sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ na wɔbɛka awarefoɔ yi ho ama wɔadi wɔn mfirinhyiada a ɛdikan wɔ wɔn ayeforɔ a wɔyɛɛ no afe a atwam no.
eng_text: At least 100 people had attended the party, in order to celebrate the first anniversary of a couple whose wedding was held last year.

text: Mpanimfoɔ de too dwa sɛ, wɔahyɛ da ato hɔ a wɔde bɛdi afahyɛ foforɔ no.
eng_text: A formal anniversary event was scheduled for a later date, officials said.

text: Na awarefoɔ no ayɛ ayeforɔ afe baako nie wɔ Texas na wɔsane baa Bufalo sɛ wɔne wɔn mfɛfoɔ ne annuanom rebɛgye wɔn ani.
eng_text: The couple had married in Texas one year ago and came to Buffalo to celebrate with friends and relatives.

text: Ayefokunu a wadi mfeɛ 30 a wɔwoo no wɔ Bufalo no yɛ nnipa nan a wɔwuuiɛ no mu baako, nanso anyɛ ne yere no ya.
eng_text: The 30-year-old husband, who was born in Buffalo, was one of the four killed in the shooting, but his wife was not hurt.

text: Karno yɛ ɔkyerɛkyerɛni a ɔkyerɛ Borɔfo a wagye din nanso ɔha adwene na ɔkyerɛɛ adeɛ wɔ Modern English ne King’s Glory na ɔtaa ka sɛ berɛ a na ɔkyerɛ adeɛ no na ɔwɔ adesuafoɔ 9,000 a wɔakyerɛ wɔn adeɛ.
eng_text: Karno is a well-known but controversial English tutor who taught under Modern Education and King's Glory who claimed to have 9,000 students at the peak of his career.

text: Wɔ n’adekyerɛ nwoma mu no, na ɔde nsɛm bi di dwuma a awofoɔ binom ka sɛ ɛnni mu papa, na ɔtaa de nsɛm fin nso di dwuma.
eng_text: In his notes he used words which some parents considered coarse, and he reportedly used profanity in class.

text: Nnɛɛmafoɔ adesua maa no daa adi pefee sɛ na ɔde nkaebɔ akɛseɛ bobɔ lɔɔre ho wɔ aberɛ a ɔnni so tumi na afei na ɔtwa ntorɔ nso sɛ ɔyɛ okunini wɔ borɔfo kasa kyerɛ mu.
eng_text: Modern Education accused him of printing large advertisements on buses without authorisation and lying by saying that he was the chief English tutor.

text: Wɔadi kan abɔ no soboɔ sɛ ɔde wawia obi dwumadie, nanso wammɔ no ka.
eng_text: He has also been accused previously of copyright infringement, but was not charged.

text: Obi a ɔwiee sukuu wɔ hɔ kaa sɛ, na ɔde Ingresifoɔ brɔfo na ɛkyerɛ adeɛ, na ɔkyerɛ mpenatweɛ ho nneɛma ma wɔktwerɛ gu wɔn nwoma mu, na wayɛ sɛ asukuufoɔ adamfo.
eng_text: A former student said that he 'used slang in class, taught dating skills in notes, and was just like the students' friend.'

text: Mfeɛ bɛyɛ ahaasa mu ni no, ɛwom sɛ wɔyɛ ɔman a wɔn ankasa di wɔ dwa deɛ, China atu mpɔn wɔ yie wɔ n’adwadie mu.
eng_text: During the last three decades, despite officially remaining a communist state, China has developed a market economy.

text: Wɔyɛɛ nsakraeɛ a ɛdi kan faa ɔman no adwadie ho berɛ a na Deng Xiaoping di wɔn so.
eng_text: The first economic reforms were made under the leadership of Deng Xiaoping.

text: Firi saa mmerɛ no, Chinaman kɛseyɛ no anyini mpɛn 90.
eng_text: Since then, China's economic size has grown by 90 times.

text: Mpɛn a ɛdi kan no, afe atwam no, China tɔn kaa kɔɔ aman foforɔ so kyɛnn Germany na wɔsane bɛsanee Amɛrika man no ho sɛ dwadibea kɛseɛ a ɛwɔ hɔ.
eng_text: For the first time, last year China exported more cars than Germany and surpassed the United States as the biggest market for this industry.

text: Mfeɛ ahaanu akyiri no, China GDP bɛtumi aboro United States deɛ so.
eng_text: China's GDP could be larger than the United States within two decades.

text: Tropical Storm Danielle, ahum a ɛtɔ so nan a wɔato no din wɔ 2010 Atlantic ‘hurricane season’ mu, asane asi bio wɔ eastern Atlantic Ocean mu.
eng_text: Tropical Storm Danielle, fourth named storm of the 2010 Atlantic hurricane season, has formed in the eastern Atlantic Ocean.

text: Ahum no a ɛsii Miami, Florida bɛyɛ 3,000 miles no, atumi agyina mframa ano bɛyɛ 40 mph (64 kph).
eng_text: The storm, located approximately 3,000 miles from Miami, Florida, has maximum sustained winds of 40 mph (64 kph).

text: Wɔn a wɔhwɛ wiem nsakraeɛ wɔ National Hurricane Center susuu sɛ, ɛmpem nkɔ si Wukuada no na Danielle ano ayɛ den adane ahum kɛseɛ.
eng_text: Scientists at the National Hurricane Center predict that Danielle will strengthen to a hurricane by Wednesday.

text: Ɛnam sɛ ahum no nya nsiiɛ nti, ɛyɛ den sɛ yɛbɛhunu ne nsunsuansoɔ a ɛde bɛba Amɛrika man anaa Caribbean so.
eng_text: As the storm is far from landfall, it remains difficult to assess potential impact to the United States or Caribbean.

text: Wɔwoo no wɔ Croatia ahenkuro, Zagreb, Bobek gyee din wɔ berɛ na ɔsi akan ma Partizan Belgrade.
eng_text: Born in the Croatian capital, Zagreb, Bobek gained fame while playing for Partizan Belgrade.

text: Ɔkɔɔ bɔɔlobɔ kuo no mu wɔ afe 1945 mu na ɔtenaa hɔ kɔsii 1958.
eng_text: He joined them in 1945 and stayed until 1958.

text: Wɔ ne pɛn so wɔ bɔɔlobɔ kuo no mu, ɔtoo ntena 403 wɔ berɛ a na wasi akan 468.
eng_text: During his time with the team, he scored 403 goals in 468 appearances.

text: Bɔɔlobɔni biara nni hɔ a wɔasi akan dodo anaa wato ntena dodo ama bɔɔlobɔ kuo no kyɛn Bobek.
eng_text: No one else has ever made more appearances or scored more goals for the club than Bobek.

text: Wɔ afe 1995 mu, wɔyii no sɛ ɔyɛ bɔɔlobɔni a ɔsombo pa ara wɔ Partizan abakɔsɛm mu.
eng_text: In 1995 he was voted the best player in Partizan's history.

text: Nwomtokuo a wɔagye din wɔ wiase nyinaa a yɛfrɛ wɔn Cirque du Soleil de dwumadiesoronko bi na ɛhyɛɛ apontoɔ no ase.
eng_text: The celebrations started with a special show by the world-renowned group Cirque du Soleil.

text: Wɔwieeɛ na Istanbul State Symphony Orchestra nso de wɔn deɛ toaa so, Janissary nwomtokuo, ne anwomtofoɔ Fatih Erkoç ne Müslüm Gürses nso ka ho.
eng_text: It was followed by the Istanbul State Symphony Orchestra, a Janissary band, and the singers Fatih Erkoç and Müslüm Gürses.

text: Whirling Dervishes kuo no nso bɛtoaa so.
eng_text: Then Whirling Dervishes took to the stage.

text: Turkey nwomtoni baa hoɔfɛfoɔ Sezen Aksu ne Italini sakubɔfoɔ Alessandro Safina ne Greek nwomtoni Haris Alexiou nso bɛtoo nwom.
eng_text: Turkish diva Sezen Aksu performed with the Italian tenor Alessandro Safina and Greek singer Haris Alexiou.

text: Deɛ wɔde twaa toɔ ne sɛ Turkey asa kuo Fire of Anatolia nso bɛdii "Troy" yɛkyerɛ dwumadie no.
eng_text: To finish, Turkish dance group Fire of Anatolia performed the show "Troy".

text: Peter Lenz, aberanteɛ a wadi mfeɛ 13 a ɔde dadepɔnkɔ si akan, anya akwanhyia awu wɔ Indianapolis Motor Speedway.
eng_text: Peter Lenz, a 13-year-old motorcycle racer, has died after being involved in a crash at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway.

text: Berɛ a na ɔrekentene ne ho wɔ kwan so no, Lenz hwee ase firi ne dadepɔnkɔ no so, na Xavier Zayat de dadepɔnkɔ twifaa ne so.
eng_text: While on his warm-up lap, Lenz fell off his bike, and was then struck by fellow racer Xavier Zayat.

text: Amonom hɔ ara na ayarehwɛfoɔ a wɔwɔ hɔ no bɛhwɛɛ no de no kɔɔ ayaresabea bi a ɛbɛn hɔ maa akyire yi ɔwuuiɛ.
eng_text: He was immediately attended to by the on-track medical staff and transported to a local hospital where he later died.

text: Zayat ampira wɔ akwanhyia no mu.
eng_text: Zayat was unhurt in the accident.

text: Ɛnam sikasɛm a ayɛ basaa wɔ waise afanaa nyinaa ho no, Zapatero toaa so kaa sɛ, "sikasɛm ka ɔman yieyɔ ho, ɛdi mu tintiman.
eng_text: Regarding the global financial situation, Zapatero continued by saying that "the financial system is a part of the economy, a crucial part.

text: Yɛwɔ sikasɛm a atɔ ape afe ni, a ano aberɛ ase bosome kakra akyi, na mehunu no sɛ seisei deɛ dwadie sikasɛm no rema ne mu so."
eng_text: We have a year-long financial crisis, which has had its most acute moment in the past two months, and I think now the financial markets are beginning to recover."

text: Nawɔtwe a ɛtwaam no, Naked News daa no adi sɛ wɔbɛpa abɛɛfo kasa ahodoɔ no bi aka ne kaseɛbɔ a wɔde to dwa ho, na wɔada kaseɛbɔ adwumakuo mmiɛnsa nso adi aka ho.
eng_text: Last week, Naked News announced that it would dramatically increase its international language mandate to news reporting, with three new broadcasts.

text: Wɔma wɔn kaseɛbɔ wɔ Brɔfo ne Japanese mu, saa dwumakuo kɛseɛ yi redane nwumadie ahodoɔ a wɔbɛka Spanish, Italian ne Korefoɔ kasa wɔ so, na wɔayi no wɔ tɛlɛbihyin, abɛɛfo ntontan ne tetefon so.
eng_text: Already reporting in English and Japanese, the global organization is launching Spanish, Italian, and Korean-language programs, for television, the web, and mobile devices.

text: Me tiri yɛɛ yie biribiara anto me, nanso mehunu adeɛ a ɛyɛ hu pa ara wɔ m’ani so, wɔ berɛ a na nkurɔfoɔ rebɔ wɔn ho mmɔden sɛ wɔbɛpae nhwehwɛ afa mu apue.
eng_text: "Luckily nothing happened to me, but I saw a macabre scene, as people tried to break windows in order to get out.

text: Na ebinom de nkonnwa rebobɔ mpoma no ano, nanso na mpoma no ntumi mmubu.
eng_text: People were hitting the panes with chairs, but the windows were unbreakable.

text: "Mpoma no baako ho buuiɛ maa wɔhyɛɛ aseɛ sɛ wɔbɛfa mu apue," wei ne nsɛm a Franciszek Kowal a ɔnyaa ne tiri didiim kaeɛ.
eng_text: One of the panes finally broke, and they started to get out by the window," said survivor Franciszek Kowal.

text: Nsroma ma yɛn kanea ne ɔhyew esiane ahoɔden a ɛda adi wɔ aberɛ a ‘hydrogen atoms’ adi afra (anaa ahyiam) redane ‘element’ a emu yɛ duru.
eng_text: Stars give off light and heat because of the energy made when hydrogen atoms are merged (or fused) together to form heavier elements.

text: Abɔdeɛ mu nyansapɛfoɔ reyɛ adwumaden a ɛbɛboa ama wɔatumi ayɛ adeɛ a ɛno nso bɛtumi ama anyinam ahoɔden.
eng_text: Scientists are working to create a reactor that can make energy in the same way.

text: Wei yɛ ɔhaw kɛseɛ a ne ko yɛ den pa ara na ɛbɛtumi adi mfeɛ bebree ansa na wɔatumi ayɛ deɛ ɛbɛdi dwuma yie.
eng_text: This, however, is a very hard problem to solve and will take many years before we see useful fusion reactors built.

text: Dadeɛ a yɛakontono no nante nsuo ani esiane nsuo ani bɔberɛ nti.
eng_text: The steel needle floats on top of the water because of surface tension.

text: Nsuo ani bɔberɛ no yɛ adwuma firisɛ, ‘molecules’ a ɛwɔ nsuo no ani no ka bom deɛ emu yɛ den sene mframa ‘molecules’ no a ɛwɔ nsuo no so no.
eng_text: Surface tension happens because the water molecules at the surface of the water are strongly attracted to each other more than they are to the air molecules above them.

text: Nsuo ‘molecules’ no yɛ honam ani adeɛ a ɛwɔ nsuo ani, na ɛma kwan ma nneɛma bi te sɛ nnadeɛ tumi nante nsuo ani.
eng_text: The water molecules make an invisible skin on the water’s surface that allows things like the needle to float on top of the water.

text: Dadebena a ɛda ‘skate’ a wɔtwi no sukɔkyea soɔ no wɔ afaafa mmienu a emu ayɛ donko. Afaa mmienu no boa ma ɛtumi kyere asukɔkyea no, wɔ berɛ akyea mu.
eng_text: The blade on a modern ice skate has a double edge with a concave hollow between them. The two edges allow for a better grasp of the ice, even when tilted.

text: Esiane sɛ dadebena no ase akoa nti, sɛ dadeɛ no kyea kɔ afa ne afa a, n’afa a ɛne asukɔkyea no nya nkutaho no so kyea.
eng_text: Because the bottom of the blade is slightly curved, as the blade tilts to one side or the other, the edge which is in contact with the ice also curves.

text: Wei na ɛboa ne ɔretwi no ma no twa ne ho. Sɛ ‘skate’ no kyea kɔ nifa a, deɛ ɔretwie no nso kɔ nifa, sɛ ɛkɔ benkum nso a, deɛ ɔretwie no nso kɔ benkum.
eng_text: This causes the skater to turn. If the skates tilt to the right, the skater turns right, if the skates tilt to the left, the skater turns left.

text: Sɛ ɛbɛtumi asane anya ahoɔden dada a na ɛwɔ no a, gye sɛ wɔgyae ahoɔden a watwe afiri kanea mu no.
eng_text: To return to their previous energy level, they must get rid of the extra energy they got from the light.

text: Wɔyɛ saa wɔ berɛ wɔreyiyi nkanea nketenkete bi adi a wɔfrɛ no "photon".
eng_text: They do this by emitting a tiny particle of light called a "photon".

text: Abɔdeɛ mu nyansapɛfoɔ frɛɛ dwumadie yi "stimulated emission of radiation" ɛfiri sɛ ‘atoms’ no nya ahoɔden firi nkanea a ɛhyerɛn mu, na ama ‘photon of light’ nso apue, ɛna kanea nso yɛ ‘radiation’ no fa bi.
eng_text: Scientists call this process "stimulated emission of radiation" because the atoms are stimulated by the bright light, causing the emission of a photon of light, and light is a type of radiation.

text: Mfonii a ɛtoa so no kyerɛ sɛnea ‘atoms’ da ‘photons’ adi. Ampa, nokorɛ mu no ‘photons’ susua sene nea ɛwɔ mfonii yi mu.
eng_text: The next picture shows the atoms emitting photons. Of course, in reality photons are a lot smaller than those in the picture.

text: ‘photons’ mpo susua sene nneɛma ɛka bom bɛdane ‘atoms’ mpo.
eng_text: Photons are even smaller than the stuff that makes up atoms!

text: Nnɔnhwere ɔha akyi a wɔyɛɛ ho adwuma no, ahoma tea a ɛhyɛ kanea no mu no hyeeɛ na kanea no antumi anyɛ adwuma bio.
eng_text: After hundreds of hours of operation the filament in the bulb eventually burns out and the light bulb no longer works.

text: Ɛba saa a na ɛhia sɛ yɛsesa kanea no. Ɛwɔ sɛ yɛyɛahwɛyie yɔ berɛ a yɛresesa kanea.
eng_text: The light bulb then needs replacing. It is necessary to be careful in replacing the light bulb.

text: Deɛ ɛi kan, ɛwɔ sɛ yɛdum adeɛ a yɛde sɔ kanea no anaa yɛtwe anyinam kanea n’ahoma no firim.
eng_text: First, the switch for the light fixture needs to be turned off or the cable disconnected.

text: Sɛnti ne sɛ, anyinam ahoɔden a ɛnam bea a yɛde sɔ kanea no a ɛyɛ dadeɛ a ɛwɔ kanea no ho no bɛtumi ama ogya afa yɛn mu wɔ berɛ a yɛn nsa akɔka saa dadeɛ no, anaa sɛ yɛn nsa akɔka dadeɛ no wɔ berɛ ɛho kakra aka bea a yɛde hyɛ mu no.
eng_text: This is because electricity flowing into the socket where the metallic part of bulb sits can give you a severe electric shock if you touch the inside of the socket or the metal base of the bulb while it is still partly in the socket.

text: Akwaa no mu deԑ ԑhia pa ara ‘aforo sane die wɔ nnipadua’ no mu ne akoma, ԑno na ԑpu mogya gu nnipadua no mu.
eng_text: The major organ of the circulatory system is the heart, which pumps the blood.

text: Mogya firi akoma no mu fa dorobԑn bi a yԑfrԑ no ‘arteries’ mu kɔ na asane afa dorobԑn a yԑfrԑ no ‘veins’ mu aba akoma no mu. Dorobԑn nketewa pa ara no din de ‘capillaries’.
eng_text: Blood goes away from the heart in tubes called arteries and comes back to the heart in tubes called veins. The smallest tubes are called capillaries.

text: ‘Triceratop’ se ntumi nwe nwura nko ara na mmom ԑtumi we dua mman ne nhini a ԑyԑ den pa ara.
eng_text: A triceratops' teeth would have been able to crush not only leaves but even very tough branches and roots.

text: Abɔdeԑ mu nyansapԑfoɔ bi dwene sԑ ‘Triceratops’ di ‘cycads’, a ԑyԑ dua bi a na ԑnyԑ nna wɔ Cretaceous.
eng_text: Some scientists think Triceratops ate cycads, which are a type of plant that was common in the Cretaceous.

text: Saa dua yi te sԑ abԑ dua ԑnna ԑwɔ nhaban a ano no yԑ feafea.
eng_text: These plants look like a small palm tree with a crown of sharp, spiky leaves.

text: Nka ‘Triceratops’ bԑtumi de n’ano denden no ayi ahaban no ansa na awe dua no ankasa.
eng_text: A Triceratops could have used its strong beak to strip off the leaves before eating the trunk.

text: Abɔdeԑ mu nyansapԑfoɔ no bi nso se saa dua yi wɔ awuduro ԑno nti ԑnyԑ adeԑ a ‘dinosaur’ biara di, ԑwom sԑ seisei ‘sloth’ ԑne mmoa bi te sԑ ako (a wɔfiri dinosaurs no ase) no tumi di nhaban anaa nnuaba a awuduro wom.
eng_text: Other scientists argue that these plants are very poisonous so it is unlikely that any dinosaur ate them, even though today the sloth and other animals like the parrot (a descendant of the dinosaurs) can eat poisonous leaves or fruit.

text: Ɛbԑyԑ dԑn na ahoɔden a ԑwɔ Io atumi atwe me? Sԑ wogyina Io ani a, wo mu duru a wowɔ no Asase so no so te.
eng_text: How would Io's gravity pull on me? If you stood on the surface of Io, you would weigh less than you do on Earth.

text: Obi a ne mu duru yԑ 200 pounds (90kg) wɔ Asase so no mu duru wɔ Io no bԑyԑ 36 pounds (16kg). Ɛno nti ahoɔden no bԑtwe wo kakra.
eng_text: A person who weighs 200 pounds (90kg) on Earth would weigh about 36 pounds (16kg) on Io. So the gravity, of course, pulls less on you.

text: Awia no nni ‘crust’ a wobԑtumi agyina so te sԑ Asase deԑ no. Awia no nyinaa yԑ ‘egyaframa’, egya, ne ‘plasma’.
eng_text: The Sun doesn't have a crust like the Earth that you can stand on. The whole Sun is made out of gases, fire, and plasma.

text: Mmerԑ dodoɔ a woretwe wo ho firi awia no ho no na ‘egyaframa’ no mu reyԑ ha.
eng_text: The gas becomes thinner as you go farther from the center of the Sun.

text: Sԑ yԑhwԑ awia no a, akyire no a yԑhunu no de ‘photosphere’, a ԑkyerԑ sԑ, "kanea kurukuruwa".
eng_text: The outer-part we see when we look at the Sun is called the photosphere, which means "ball of light".

text: Mfeԑ mpem mmiԑnsa akyi no, afe 1610 mu no, ‘Italian astronomer Galileo Galilei’ de ‘telescope’ hunuu sԑ, Venus wɔ nkyekyԑmu bi te sԑ deԑ bosome wɔ no.
eng_text: About three thousand years later, in 1610, Italian astronomer Galileo Galilei used a telescope to observe that Venus has phases, just as the moon does.

text: Saa nkyekyԑmu yi ba ԑfiri sԑ Venus (anaa Bosome) no fa a ԑkyerԑ Awia no nko ara na ԑnya kanea. Venus nkyekyԑmu yi kaa bi too ‘Copernicus adwenkyerԑ’ so sԑ ‘planets’ no twa Awia ho hyia.
eng_text: Phases happen because only the side of Venus (or of the Moon) facing the Sun is lighted. The phases of Venus supported the theory of Copernicus that the planets go around the Sun.

text: Mfeԑ kakra bi akyire 1639 no, ‘English astronomer a ɔde Jeremiah Horrocks’ hunuu sԑ Venus firi baabi kɔ baabi.
eng_text: Then, a few years later in 1639, an English astronomer named Jeremiah Horrocks observed a transit of Venus.

text: Na England san dii Danelaw so nkonim no, onyaa asomdwoe pii bere tenten.
eng_text: England had experienced a long period of peace after the reconquest of the Danelaw.

text: Nanso, wɔ afe 991 mu no Ethelred hyiaa Viking a na ne dɔm no dɔɔso paa kyɛn dɔm biara no, efiri Guthrum deɛ no so, bɛyɛ mfe apem a na aba kɔ no.
eng_text: However in 991 Ethelred was faced with a Viking fleet larger than any since Guthrum's a century earlier.

text: Nea na odi saa dɔm no anim ne Olaf Trygvasson, Norwayni a na ne botae ne sɛ ɔbɛgye ne man afiri Danefo no nnisoɔ ase.
eng_text: This fleet was led by Olaf Trygvasson, a Norwegian with ambitions to reclaim his country from Danish domination.

text: Wɔ asraafo no nkuguo a edi kan no akyi no, Ethelred tumi ne Olaf yɛɛ nhehyɛe, na ɔsan kɔɔ Norway kɔbɔɔ mmɔden sɛ ne nsa bɛka n'ahinni no. Ɛyɛɛ te sɛ nkunim ne nkuguo a adi afrafra.
eng_text: After initial military setbacks, Ethelred was able to agree to terms with Olaf, who returned to Norway to try to gain his kingdom with mixed success.

text: Hangeul nko ara ne atwerԑdeԑ a wɔde baeԑ a wɔde di dwuma da biara. Saa atwerԑdeԑ yi bae wɔafe 1444 mu Ɔhene Sejong ahennie berԑ so (1418 – 1450).
eng_text: Hangeul is the only purposely invented alphabet in popular daily use. The alphabet was invented in 1444 during the reign of King Sejong (1418 – 1450).

text: Na Ɔhene Sejong yԑ ɔhene a ɔtɔ so nnan wɔ Joseon Dynasty no mu ԑnna ɔyԑ obi a wɔbu no pa ara.
eng_text: King Sejong was the fourth king of the Joseon Dynasty and is one of the most highly regarded.

text: Ɔdii kan too Hangeul atwerԑdeԑ no din Hunmin Jeongeum, a ԑkyerԑ sԑ "nnyegyeeԑ pa no a yԑde tenetene ɔmanfoɔ no".
eng_text: He originally named the Hangeul alphabet Hunmin Jeongeum, which means "the correct sounds for the instruction of the people".

text: Adwenkyerԑ bebree wɔ hɔ fa kwan a Sanskrit faa so baeԑ ho. Wɔn mu baako fa ‘Aryan akwantuo’ a wɔde firi atɔeԑ wuraa India mu a na wɔde wɔn kasa nam ho.
eng_text: There are many theories to how Sanskrit came into existence. One of them is about an Aryan migration from the west into India who brought their language with them.

text: Sanskrit yԑ tete kasa na yԑbԑtumi de atoto Latin kasa a wɔka no wɔ Europe no ho.
eng_text: Sanskrit is an ancient language and is comparable to the Latin language spoken in Europe.

text: Tete nwoma a na ԑwɔ wiase no nyinaa na wɔatwerԑ no Sanskrit kasa mu. Wɔkekaa ‘Upanishads’ sii ani wieeԑ no, Sanskrit yerae ԑnam tumi nnidisoɔ nti.
eng_text: The earliest known book in the world was written in Sanskrit. After the compilation of Upanishads, Sanskrit just faded due to hierarchy.

text: Sanskrit yԑ kasa a ԑyԑ den na ԑyԑ dԑ a ԑno ne India kasa bebree farebae, sԑdeԑ Latin nso yԑ Europe kasa bi te sԑ French ne Spanish farebae no.
eng_text: Sanskrit is a very complex and rich language, which has served to be the source for many modern Indian languages, just like Latin is the source for European languages like French and Spanish.

text: Berԑ a wɔne France ntɔkwa no baa awieeԑ no, Germany yԑԑ ahoboa sԑ wɔbԑto ahyԑ Britain so.
eng_text: With the battle for France over, Germany began to get ready to invade the island of Britain.

text: Germany too saa ɔsa yi din “Operation Sealion”. Britain asogyafoɔ no akodeԑ bebree yerae berԑ a wɔtu firii Dunkirk no nti na wɔayԑ mmrԑ.
eng_text: Germany code-named the attack “Operation Sealion”. Most of the British Army's heavy weapons and supplies had been lost when it evacuated from Dunkirk, so the army was fairly weak.

text: Nanso na Roya Navy no da so wɔ ahoɔden sene German Navy no (“Kriegsmarine”) a sԑ obiara bԑto hyԑԑ English Channel no so a, anka wɔbԑdi ne so nkonim.
eng_text: But the Royal Navy was still much stronger than the German Navy (“Kriegsmarine”) and could have destroyed any invasion fleet sent across the English Channel.

text: Nanso na Roya Navy no suhyԑn no kakra bi na na ԑwɔ baabi a atamfo no bԑfa aba ԑfiri sԑ na akannifoɔ no suro sԑ German de akodeԑ firi soro bԑha wɔn.
eng_text: However, very few Royal Navy ships were based near the likely invasion routes as the admirals were afraid they would be sunk by German air attack.

text: Ma yԑnhyԑ aseԑ mfiri Italy nhyehyԑeԑ no nkyerԑmu no ho. Na Italy yԑ Germany ne Japan "nuabarima ketewa".
eng_text: Let's start with an explanation about Italy's plans. Italy was mainly the "little brother" of Germany and Japan.

text: Na wɔn asogyafoɔ ne navy no nni ahoɔden, ԑwom sԑ na wɔayԑ suhyԑn mono nnan ansa naɔ ko no rehyԑ aseԑ.
eng_text: It had a weaker army and a weaker navy, although they had just built four new ships right before the beginning of the war.

text: Na deԑ Italy repԑ nyinaa ne Afrika aman. Sԑ wɔbԑtumi anya saa aman yi a, na wɔhia sԑ wɔnya akofoɔ a wɔbԑfa ԑpo no so saa de abԑwura Afrika.
eng_text: Italy's main goals were African countries. To capture those countries, they would need to have a troop launching pad, so as troops could sail across the Mediterranean Sea and invade Africa.

text: Ɛno nti, na ԑsԑ sԑ wɔyi baabi a Britain wɔ ne wɔn suhyԑn a ԑwɔ Egypt no nyinaa firi hɔ. Sԑ wɔyi saa adeԑ yi to nkyԑn a, na ԑnni sԑ Italy akofoɔ no yԑ biribi foforɔ biara.
eng_text: For that, they had to get rid of British bases and ships in Egypt. Besides those actions, Italy's battleships were not supposed to do anything else.

text: Afei Japan. Na asuo atwa Japan ho ahyia te sԑ Britain.
eng_text: Now for Japan. Japan was an island country, just like Britain.

text: ‘Submarines’ yԑ suhyԑn a wɔayԑ sԑ ԑmfa asuo ase, na ԑnwɔ hɔ berԑ bi mu.
eng_text: Submarines are ships designed to travel underwater, and remain there for an extended amount of time.

text: Wɔde ‘Submarines’ dii dwuma wɔ Wiase Ntɔkwa kɛseɛ I ԑne Wiase Ntɔkwa kɛseɛ II’ no mu. Saa berԑ no na ԑyԑ nyaa ԑnna ԑsane nso wɔ baabi pɔtee a ԑtumi to tuo kɔduru.
eng_text: Submarines were used in World War I and World War II. Back then they were very slow and had a very limited shooting range.

text: Ɔko no ahyԑaseԑ no na wɔtaa fa asuo no ani, nanso berԑ rekɔ n’anim no ‘submarines’ no kɔɔ asuo no ase sԑdeԑ ԑbԑyԑ a wɔnhu wɔn.
eng_text: In the beginning of the war they mostly travelled on top of the sea, but as radar began developing and becoming more accurate the submarines were forced to go under water to avoid being seen.

text: Na wɔfrԑ German ‘submarines’ no U-Boats. Na Germanfoɔ no ayԑ adeԑ wɔ kwan a wɔfa so de ‘submarines’ di dwuma no ho.
eng_text: German submarines were called U-Boats. The Germans were very good at navigating and operating their submarines.

text: Ɛnam kwan a na wɔfa so de ‘submarines’ no di dwuma yie no nti, ɔko no akyi no wɔannye Germanfoɔ no anni sԑ wɔwɔ bebree.
eng_text: Because of their success with submarines, after the war Germans aren't trusted to have many of them.

text: Aane! Ɔhene Tutankhamun, a ԑtɔ da a wɔtumi frԑ no "King Tut" anaa "The Boy King", yԑ tete Egypt ahemfo no mu baako a wɔnim no berԑ yi mu.
eng_text: Yes! King Tutankhamun, sometimes referred to as "King Tut" or "The Boy King", is one of the most well known ancient Egyptian kings in modern times.

text: Deԑ ԑyԑ nwanwa ne sԑ na wɔnhu no sԑ ne ho hia tete mmerԑ no mu nti wɔantwerԑ ne ho asԑm tete ahemfo nwoma bebree mu.
eng_text: Interestingly, he was not considered to be very important in ancient times and was not recorded on most ancient king lists.

text: Nanso berԑ a wɔhuu ne nna afe 1922 mu no ԑmaa nnipa huu no yie. Akorɔmfoɔ wiaa nna bebree mu adeԑ nanso ne deԑ no nko ara deԑ, wɔamfa wɔn nsa anka.
eng_text: However, the discovery of his tomb in 1922 made him a celebrity. While many tombs of the past were robbed, this tomb was left virtually undisturbed.

text: Na nneԑma a wɔde siee Tutankhamun no bebree a wɔhɔ a ԑnyԑԑ hwee, a nneԑma a wɔde sika kɔkɔɔ ne aboɔ a ԑho hia ayԑ mpempem ka ho.
eng_text: Most of the items buried with Tutankhamun have been well preserved, including thousands of artefacts made from precious metals and rare stones.

text: ‘Spoke wheels’ a Assyriafoɔ no yԑeԑ no maa wɔn apɔnkɔ no mu yԑԑ ha sane ho yԑԑ hare a na wɔbԑtumi asane asogyafoɔ ne apɔnkɔfoforɔ ho.
eng_text: The invention of spoke wheels made Assyrian chariots lighter, faster, and better prepared to outrun soldiers and other chariots.

text: Na wɔn pea no tumi wura asogyafoɔ a wɔne wɔn reko no akokyԑm no mu. Bԑyԑ 1000 B.C., Assyriafoɔ de ‘cavalry’ a ԑdi kan no baeԑ.
eng_text: Arrows from their deadly crossbows could penetrate the armor of rival soldiers. About 1000 B.C., the Assyrians introduced the first cavalry.

text: ‘Cavalry’ yԑ asogyafoɔ a wɔtena apɔnkɔ akyi di ako. Saa berԑ no na wɔnyԑԑ ‘deԑ wɔde gu pɔnkɔ akyi’ no nti na wɔtena apɔnkɔ no akyi saa ara na wɔdi ako no.
eng_text: A cavalry is an army that fights on horseback. The saddle had not yet been invented, so the Assyrian cavalry fought on the bare backs of their horses.

text: Yԑnim Greek amanyɔfoɔ, abɔdeԑ mu paadehunufoɔ, mfoninyԑfoɔ bebree. Ebia wɔn mu deԑ yԑnim no pa ara ne Homer, onifrani a na ɔka anwonsԑm no a ɔyԑԑ Greek kasadwini mmienu: ‘the poems Iliad ԑne Odyssey’ no.
eng_text: We know many Greek politicians, scientists, and artists. Possibly the most known person of this culture is Homer, the legendary blind poet, who composed two masterpieces of Greek literature: the poems Iliad and Odyssey.

text: ‘Sophocles ԑne Aristophanes’ yԑ wɔn a wɔtwerԑ ahwԑgorɔ nwoma a wɔwɔ din pa ara na wɔn ahwԑgorɔ ka wiase kasadwini a ԑdi mu pa ara no ho bi.
eng_text: Sophocles and Aristophanes are still popular playwrights and their plays are considered to be among the greatest works of world literature.

text: Greekni a wagye din bio yԑ ‘mathematician Pythagoras’, a dodoɔ no ara nim no sԑ ɔde ayɔnkofa a ԑda ‘triangle’ afaafa no ntam no baeԑ no.
eng_text: Another famous Greek is a mathematician Pythagoras, mostly known for his famous theorem about relations of the sides of right triangles.

text: Nnipa dodoɔ a wɔka Hindi no sesa. Wɔkyerԑ sԑ ԑyԑ ԑfiri mmienu kɔsi nnan mu kasa a nnipa dodoɔ ka pa ara wɔ wiase.
eng_text: There are varying estimates for how many people speak Hindi. It is estimated to be between the second and fourth most commonly spoken language in the world.

text: Nnipa dodoɔ a wɔfiri kuro no mu ka kasa no sesa a ne nnyinasoɔ no yԑ nkorabata a wɔkan no.
eng_text: The number of native speakers varies depending on whether or not very closely related dialects are counted.

text: Nnipa dodoɔ a wɔde wɔn ani bu sԑ wɔka kasa no yԑ bԑyԑ ɔpepem 340 kɔsi ɔpepem 500, ԑnna wɔn a wɔte no yԑ ɔpepem 800.
eng_text: Estimates range from 340 million to 500 million speakers, and as many as 800 million people can understand the language.

text: Hindi ԑne Urdu sԑ wɔn sԑmfua a ԑde di dwuma mu nanso atwerԑ mu deԑ, ԑsesa; nnipa a wɔka kasa no mmienu bԑtumi ate wɔn ho ase wɔ daadaa nkɔmmɔdie mu.
eng_text: Hindi and Urdu are similar in vocabulary but different in script; in everyday conversations, speakers of both languages can usually understand each other.

text: Mfeɛ ɔha a ɛtɔ so 15th mu hɔ no, na ‘Estonia Atifi fam’ hyԑ Germany amanneԑ ase.
eng_text: Around the 15th century, northern Estonia was under great cultural influence of Germany.

text: Na Germanfoɔ bi pԑ sԑ wɔka Onyankopɔn ho asԑm kyerԑ nnipa no, ԑno nti wɔyԑԑ ‘Estonian literal language’ no.
eng_text: Some German monks wanted to bring God closer to the native people, so they invented the Estonian literal language.

text: Na ne nnyinasoɔ yԑ German atwerԑdeԑ no ԑnna wɔde atwerԑdeԑ baako yi "Õ/õ" kaa ho.
eng_text: It was based on the German alphabet and one character "Õ/õ" was added.

text: Mmerԑ bi akyi no nsԑmfua bebree a wɔfԑm firii German kasa mu bԑnyaa nteaseԑ. Wei ne anibue ahyԑaseԑ.
eng_text: As time passed, many words that were borrowed from German coalesced. This was the beginning of enlightenment.

text: Amammerԑ kwan so no, deԑ ɔbԑdi adeԑ no wura sogya mu berԑ a wawie sukuu no.
eng_text: Traditionally, the heir to the throne would go straight into the military after finishing school.

text: Nanso, Charles kɔɔ suapɔn wɔTrinity College, Cambridge ԑhɔ na ɔsuaa ‘Anthropology ԑne Archaeology’, ԑne ‘History’ akyire yi, a ɔnyaa 2:2 (suapɔn abodin a yɛfrɛ no).
eng_text: However, Charles went to university at Trinity College, Cambridge where he studied Anthropology and Archaeology, and later History, earning a 2:2 (a lower second class degree).

text: Charles ne onipa a ɔdi kan wɔ Britania Adehye Abusua no mu a ɔnyaa abodin krataa.
eng_text: Charles was the first member of the British Royal Family to be awarded a degree.

text: 'European Turkey (eastern Thrace or Rumelia in the Balkan peninsula) yԑ ɔman no mu 3%.
eng_text: European Turkey (eastern Thrace or Rumelia in the Balkan peninsula) includes 3% of the country.

text: Turkey ano bԑboro 1,600 kilometres (1,000 mi) wɔ ne tenten mu ԑne 800 km (500 mi) wɔ ne tԑtrԑtԑ mu, akɔyԑ ‘rectangular shape’.
eng_text: The territory of Turkey is more than 1,600 kilometres (1,000 mi) long and 800 km (500 mi) wide, with a roughly rectangular shape.

text: Turkey beaeԑ no wɔ weinom ka ho ‘lakes, ԑfa 783,562 square kilometres (300,948 sq mi), a emu 755,688 square kilometres (291,773 sq mi) wɔ Asia anaafoɔ atɔeԑ ԑnna 23,764 square kilometres (9,174 sq mi) wɔ Europe’.
eng_text: Turkey's area, including lakes, occupies 783,562 square kilometres (300,948 sq mi), of which 755,688 square kilometres (291,773 sq mi) are in south west Asia and 23,764 square kilometres (9,174 sq mi) in Europe.

text: Turkey beaeԑ no ma no yԑ wiase mu ɔman a ԑtɔ so 37 a ԑso pa ara, ԑnna ԑreyԑ ne ‘Metropolitan France ԑne the United Kingdom’ a yԑaka abom ayԑ pԑ.
eng_text: Turkey's area makes it the world's 37th-largest country, and is about the size of Metropolitan France and the United Kingdom combined.

text: Ɛpo atwa Turkey ho ahyia wɔ baabi mmiԑnsa: ‘Aegean Sea no wɔ atɔeԑ, Black Sea no wɔ atifi ԑnna Mediterranean Sea no wɔ anaafoɔ.
eng_text: Turkey is encircled by seas on three sides: the Aegean Sea to the west, the Black Sea to the north and the Mediterranean Sea to the south.

text: Luxembourg wↄ abakↄsεm tenten nanso wↄn ahofadie afe a efi 1839 nka ho.
eng_text: Luxembourg has a long history but its independence dates from 1839.

text: Na εnnε bere wei mu Belgiunm fa bi ka Luxembourg ho tete no nanso εbεyε sε Belgium wↄ 1830 Belgian Revolution.
eng_text: Present-day parts of Belgium were part of Luxembourg in the past but became Belgian after the 1830s Belgian Revolution.

text: Luxembourg man no bↄ wↄn ho mmↄden sε wↄnngyina ↄfa biara nanso Germany man no mu wↄde wↄn ho hyε Wiase Nyinaa Ko I ne Wiase Nyinaa Ko II no mu.
eng_text: Luxembourg has always tried to remain a neutral country but it was occupied in both World War I and World War II by Germany.

text: Wↄ afe 1957 mu no, Luxemburg bεyεε aman a wↄtee kuo bi a εnnε wↄfrε no European Union.
eng_text: In 1957 Luxembourg became a founding member of the organization which is today known as the European Union.

text: Drukgyal Dzong yε abankεseε a adane dantuo na esane yↄ Buddahfoↄ ahotefoↄ efie a εwↄ Paro ↄmansini no atififam (wↄ Phondey Akuraseε).
eng_text: The Drukgyal Dzong is a ruined fortress and Buddhist monastery in the upper part of the Paro District (in Phondey Village).

text: Wↄka sε wↄ afe 1649 mu no, Zhabdrung Ngaawang Namgyel yε abankεseε no maa nkonim a odii wↄ Tibetan_mongol asrafoↄ so no.
eng_text: It is said that in 1649, Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyel created the fortress to commemorate his victory against the Tibetan-Mongol forces.

text: Wↄ afe 1951 mu no, ogyahyehyε bi siia nnoↄma nyinaa hyeeε nanso tete Drukgyal Zhabdrung Ngawang nnoↄma no kaa yε, ebi yε Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyal ahoni no.
eng_text: In 1951, a fire caused for only some of the relics of the Drukgyal Dzong to remain, such as the image of Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyal.

text: Ogyahyehyε no akyi no, wↄ koraa abankεseε no so na wↄbↄↄ ho ban nso, εno ma no bεyεε Bhutan ade a εtwetwe amanfoↄ na εmaa wↄn ahomeka.
eng_text: After the fire, the fortress was preserved and protected, remaining to be one of Bhutan's most sensational attractions.

text: Wↄ mfe mpem ahawↄtwe bere mu no Cambodia man no bεhyε aman mmienu a wↄwↄ tumi paa ntamu, Thailand ne Vietnam.
eng_text: During the 18th century Cambodia found itself squeezed between two powerful neighbors, Thailand and Vietnam.

text: Thailandfoↄ no to hyε Cambodia man no so mpεn pii wↄ mfe mmpem ahawↄtwe bere no mu na 1772 mu no wↄ sεe Phom Phen.
eng_text: The Thais invaded Cambodia several times in the 18th century and in 1772 they destroyed Phnom Phen.

text: Wↄ mfe a etwa toↄ wↄ mfe mpem ahawↄtwe bere mu no Vietnamfoↄ no nso to hyεε Cambodia so.
eng_text: In the last years of the 18th century the Vietnamese also invaded Cambodia.

text: Venezuelafoↄ ↄha mu nkekyemu duowↄtwe na wↄn nyε adwuma, na wↄn a wↄyε adwuma no nso yε nnwuma a εnhyε aban aseε.
eng_text: Eighteen percent of Venezuelans are unemployed, and most of those who are employed work in the informal economy.

text: Venezuelafoↄ mu mmienu mu nkekyemu mmiεnsa a wↄyε adwuma no yε ↄsom adwuma, bεyε nkyeyemu anan yε adwuma wↄ adwumayε beaε a wↄ danedane asase so nnoↄma ani na nkyeyemu anum yε kuayↄ adwuma.
eng_text: Two thirds of Venezuelans who work do so in the service sector, nearly a quarter work in industry and a fifth work in agriculture.

text: Asase so nnoↄma a εsomboↄ paa ma Venezuelafoↄ no yε ngo, na ↄman no de emufa kεseε tu kwan kↄ nkuro foforↄ so, emfa ho sε wↄn mu ↄha mu nkekyemu baako pε na εyↄ adwuma wↄ ngo ho adwumayε beaε hↄ.
eng_text: An important industry for Venezuelans is oil, where the country is a net exporter, even though only one percent work in the oil industry.

text: Wↄ ↄman no ahofadie mfiaseε no, Singapore Botanic turo ho nimdiefoↄ boa ma wↄ sesaa nsuopↄw no bεyεε no Garden City asase a εhye wↄ so.
eng_text: Early in the nation's independence, Singapore Botanic Gardens' expertise helped to transform the island into a tropical Garden City.

text: Wↄ afe 1981 no wↄ faa, Vanda Miss Joaquim, orchid nhwiren, sε ↄman no nhwiren.
eng_text: In 1981, Vanda Miss Joaquim, an orchid hybrid, was chosen as the nation's national flower.

text: Afe biara no wↄ Ahinime mu no mmoa a wↄwe ahaban ↄpepem baako ne aha num tu kↄ anaafoↄ asase pradadaa so, na wↄtwa Mara Asubↄnten, firi atififam bepↄ so nsuo no enti.
eng_text: Every year around October nearly 1.5 million herbivores travel towards the southern plains, crossing the Mara River, from the northern hills for the rains.

text: Na wↄnam atↄeεfam san ba atififam, na wↄ san twa Mara asubↄnten no ba, nsuo tↄ no akyiri wↄ Oforisuo mu.
eng_text: And then back to the north through the west, once again crossing the Mara river, after the rains in around April.

text: Serengeti man no mmoa tenabea wↄ Serengeti mantemu, mmoa tenabea a εwↄ Ngorongoro ne Maswa mmoa tenabea a εwↄ Tanzania ne Maasai Mara man no mmoa tenabea wↄ Kenya.
eng_text: The Serengeti region contains the Serengeti National Park, the Ngorongoro Conservation Area and Maswa Game Reserve in Tanzania and the Maasai Mara National Reserve in Kenya.

text: Dawurubↄ mu nkotahodie ho adesua hwehwε sε wotumi nya nkↄmmↄ ne amammerε ho nimdeε, saa nso na εsε sε wonya nnwinade a wosua wↄ adesuadan mu no nso ho nimdeε paa (anansesεm a wↄkyerεw wↄ kyerεwpon so, ↄbↄtie ne ↄhwεtie mu nyiyimu, anasesεm ka, ne neaε εkeka ho.)
eng_text: Learning to create interactive media requires conventional and traditional skills, as well as tools mastered in interactive classes (storyboarding, audio and video editing, story telling, etc.)

text: Nkↄmmↄbↄ ho bↄtirimuyε hwehwε sε wo san susu dea wodwene fa dawurubↄ adwuma ho na wosua sε wobεdwene nnoↄma ho wↄ akwan ahodoↄ so.
eng_text: Interactive design requires that you re-assess your assumptions about media production and learn to think in a non-linear ways.

text: Nkↄmmↄbↄ ho bↄtirimyε hwehwε sε nhyehyεeε ho nnoↄma nyinaa hyia, nanso εsε sε ne nyinaa yε adeε a nyansa wↄ mu sε woyiyi no baako baako a.
eng_text: Interactive design requires that components of a project connect to each other, but also make sense as a separate entity.

text: Ↄhaw a εwↄ zoom mfoninitwa nhwehwε ho yε ne focal ho adwuma a εyε bisibasa ne mfoninitwa ahwehwε ho nnoↄma a εho hia na watumi anya focal ntwemu a εwↄ anim sen mfoninitwa nhwehwε a εba fam deε.
eng_text: The disadvantage of zoom lenses is that the focal complexity and number of lens elements required to achieve a range of focal lengths is much greater than for prime lenses.

text: Saa ↄhaw wei abεyε ↄhaw ketewa ama wↄn a wↄyε mfoninitwa ahwehwε efiri sε wↄtumi yε mfoninitwa ahwehwε a εyε papa.
eng_text: This is becoming less of an issue as lens manufacturers achieve higher standards in lens production.

text: Wei ama zoom mfoninitwa ahwehwε no tumi ma mfonini yεfε paa te sε dea wↄde mfoninitwa ahwehwε a εwↄ focal ntwemu pↄtee na etwaaeε.
eng_text: This has allowed zoom lenses to produce pictures of a quality comparable to that achieved by lenses with fixed focal length.

text: Ↄhaw foforↄ a εwↄ zoom mfonintwa nhwehwε ho ne sε akwan a kanea famu (ahoↄhareε) no εtae wↄ fam.
eng_text: Another disadvantage of zoom lenses is that the maximum aperture (the speed) of the lens is usually lower.
