text: Wei ma no yε den sε wode zoom mfoninitwa nhwehwε a ne bo wↄ fam no betwa mfonini wↄ beaε a kanea nni anaa kanea εwↄ fam.
eng_text: This makes inexpensive zoom lenses hard to use in low-light conditions without a flash.

text: Ɔhaw baako a wɔtaa hyia bere a wode sini rekɔ DVD so no ne sɛ mfoni no fa bi kɔtɛ nkyɛn bere a worebɔ no.
eng_text: One of the most common problems when trying to convert a movie to DVD format is the overscan.

text: TV ahodoɔ pii wɔ hɔ a wɔyɛ de sɔ ɔmanfoɔ pii no ani.
eng_text: Most televisions are made in a way to please the general public.

text: Eno nti, biribiara a wohu wɔ TV so no wɔ ɛhyeɛ a atwa wɔ soro, fam, ne nkyɛn nkyɛn.
eng_text: For that reason, everything you see on the TV had the borders cut, top, bottom and sides.

text: Wɔyɛ saa de ma mfoni no nyinaa kata anim. Brɔfo kasa mu no wɔfrɛ no "overscan", a ase kyerɛ sɛ mfoni no bi kɔtɛ ɛfa bere a worebɔ no.
eng_text: This is made to ensure that the image covers the whole screen. That is called overscan.

text: Nanso, sɛ woyɛ DVD a, ebia wobetwa ne hyeɛ nso. Na sɛ sini no wɔ nkyrɔeɛ a ɛbɛn aseɛ hɔ pii a, ne nyinaa ɛmma yiye.
eng_text: Unfortunately, when you make a DVD, it's borders will most likely be cut too, and if the video had subtitles too close to the bottom, they won't be fully shown.

text: Tete abakɔsɛm no ma deɛ yɛsusu no di nhini, ɛkaekae yɛn mfonii a ɛfa ako, nnipa dodoɔ bi apontoɔ ne ɔhenepɔn Arthur ho.
eng_text: The traditional medieval castle has long inspired the imagination, conjuring up images of jousts, banquets and Arthurian chivalry.

text: Ɛmfa ho mpo sɛ atumi agyina ɔsɛeɛ ano mfeɛ apem, ɛnyɛ den sɛ yɛbɛtwe yɛn adwene asi ako a asisi tete so, na yɛate nan a ɛkeka bom wɔ akwan so na huboa abɔ yɛn ɛnam afiase da nti.
eng_text: Even standing amidst thousand year-old ruins it is easy to bring to mind the sounds and smells of battles long gone, to almost hear the clatter of hooves on the cobbles and to smell the fear rising from the dungeon pits.

text: Nanso deɛ yɛdwene ho no gyina deɛ asie so? Adɛn nti na wɔsisii abankɛseɛ? Sɛn na wɔsi hyehyɛeɛ na wɔsii no?
eng_text: But is our imagination based on reality? Why were castles built in the first place? How were they designed and built?

text: Wↄ saa bere titire no, Kirby Muxloe Abankεseε no yε ↄdan a wↄn ahyεmu den sen abankεseε no ankasa.
eng_text: Typical for the period, Kirby Muxloe Castle is more of a fortified house than a true castle.

text: Ne mpoma a wↄde ahwehwε ayε ne fasuo teatea no rentumi nnyina nhyεso ano nkyε.
eng_text: Its large glazed windows and thin walls would not have been able to resist a determined attack for long.

text: Wↄ 1480 bere mu, bere a Lord Hastings fii ase sii no, na ↄman no wↄ asomdwoe na na nkuo nketewa ne atuatefoↄ ho nkoa na na wohia ahobanmↄ.
eng_text: In the 1480s, when its construction was begun by Lord Hastings, the country was relatively peaceful and defense was only required against small bands of roving marauders.

text: Na tumi a wↄkyε no pεpεεpε no yε akwanso adeyↄ a Europe man no fa so ma Europe nkuro no nyinaa tumi a wↄwↄ no tena hↄ.
eng_text: The balance of power was a system in which European nations sought to maintain the national sovereignty of all European states.

text: Na atrimupↄ ne sε Europe aman nyinaa bεhwε sε ↄman baako rengye tumidie no nyinaa, ne saa enti na aman no mu aban tae sesa kuo a wↄwↄ mu sεnea εbεyε a bribiara bεyε pε.
eng_text: The concept was that all European nations had to seek to prevent one nation from becoming powerful, and thus national governments often changed their alliances in order to maintain the balance.

text: Spain Ahindie ho Ↄko no hyεε ↄko a edi kan a na εfa tumidie a εbε kari pε no ho agyirae.
eng_text: The War of Spanish Succession marked the first war whose central issue was the balance of power.

text: Wei hyεε nsakraε kεseε hi agyirae, efirisε Europe man no tumidie no renngyina ↄsom so nko bio. Enti, mfe Aduasa Ↄko no bεyε ↄko a etwa to a wↄbεferε no ↄsom ho ↄko.
eng_text: This marked an important change, as European powers would no longer have the pretext of being religious wars. Thus, the Thirty Years' War would be the last war to be labeled a religious war.

text: Artemis asↄrefie a εwↄ Ephesus no wↄseε no wↄ Kitawonsa 21, 356 BCE bere a Herostratusfoↄ no twaa ogya too mu no.
eng_text: The temple of Artemis at Ephesus was destroyed on July 21, 356 BCE in an act of arson committed by Herostratus.

text: Abakↄsεm kyerε sε, dea na εhyε no nkuran ne sε ↄbɛdi nkonim ↄkwan biara so. Ephesofpↄ no, abufuo mu no, kaeε sε mma wↄn twerε Herostratus din da.
eng_text: According to the story, his motivation was fame at any cost. The Ephesians, outraged, announced that Herostratus' name never be recorded.

text: Greek abakↄsεm twerεfoↄ Strado twerɛ edin no, εno na yenim εnnε no. Wↄseε asↄrefie no saa anadwo a wↄwoo Alexander the Great no.
eng_text: The Greek historian Strabo later noted the name, which is how we know today. The temple was destroyed on the same night that Alexander the Great was born.

text: Alexander, a ↄyε ↄhene no, yεe sε anka obetua sika ama wↄn asan asi asↄrefie no bio, nanso wↄn angye saa adeyε no anto mu. Ekyiri yi, wↄ Alexander wuo akyi no, wↄ san sii asↄrefie no wↄ 323 BCE mu.
eng_text: Alexander, as king, offered to pay to rebuild the temple, but his offer was denied. Later, after Alexander died, the temple was rebuilt in 323 BCE.

text: Bↄ mmↄden sε wonsa ntea ho be dwodwo wↄ abereε a womia nnwomto mu agyire no so yiyie no - afei nso bↄ mmɔden sε wommfa wo nsa tea no nnyε adwuma den biara.
eng_text: Make sure your hand is as relaxed as possible while still hitting all the notes correctly - also try not to make much extraneous motion with your fingers.

text: Woyε no sa a, woremmerε pii. Kae sε εho nhia sε wo bɛmia mmia no so den dodo sε enyε dede kεseε te sε piano no.
eng_text: This way, you will tire yourself out as little as possible. Remember there's no need to hit the keys with a lot of force for extra volume like on the piano.

text: Wↄ senkuo no so no, sε ano bεyε den bi aka ho a, mia bellows no so den anaa mia so ntεmntεm.
eng_text: On the accordion, to get extra volume, you use the bellows with more pressure or speed.

text: Mysticism ɛyɛ hu a obi behu twaka a ɛda obi ne adeɛ bi ntam, hu a obehu ne ho ne adeɛ bi, anaa sɛ obi be hu dea ɛwɔ hɔ ankasa, sɛdeɛ biribi kyɛn so, honhom ho nokware, anaa Onyankopɔn.
eng_text: Mysticism is the pursuit of communion with, identity with, or conscious awareness of an ultimate reality, divinity, spiritual truth, or God.

text: Ɔgyedini no hwԑ sԑ ɔbԑnya suahunu anaa nhunumu wɔ nyame bi/bosom bi mu.
eng_text: The believer seeks a direct experience, intuition, or insight into divine reality/the deity or dieties.

text: Akyidifoɔ no bɔ wɔn bra kwan bi so anaa nneԑma bi a ԑma saa suahunu no kɔ nkan.
eng_text: Followers pursue certain ways of living, or practices that are intended to nurture those experiences.

text: Deԑ ԑma ‘Mysticism’ da nso firi ԑsom foforɔ ho ne suahunu a wɔsi so dua sԑ obi nya wɔ berԑ a ɔde n’adwene asi so ne titire ne asomdwoeԑ, nhunumu, nhyira anaa anigyeԑ mmorosoɔ so no.
eng_text: Mysticism can be distinguished from other forms of religious belief and worship by its emphasis on the direct personal experience of a unique state of consciousness, particularly those of a peaceful, insightful, blissful, or even ecstatic character.

text: ‘Sikhism’ yԑ som a ԑfiri ‘India’. Ɛhyԑԑ aseԑ firii ‘Punjab’ mpɔtam hɔ wɔ ‘15th mfeɛ ɔha a ɛtɔ so berԑ no mu wɔ berԑ a nkyekyԑmu baa ‘Hindu amammerԑ’ mu no.
eng_text: Sikhism is a religion from the Indian sub-continent. It originated in the Punjab region during the 15th century from a sectarian split within the Hindu tradition.

text: ‘Sikhs’ no hunu wɔn som no sԑ ԑne ‘Hinduism’ no nyԑ pԑ ԑwom sԑ wɔgye tom sԑ ԑfiri ‘Hindu amammerԑ’ mu na ԑbaeԑ.
eng_text: Sikhs consider their faith to be a separate religion from Hinduism though they acknowledge its Hindu roots and traditions.

text: ‘Sikhs’ no frԑ wɔn som no ‘Gurmat’ a ԑyԑ Punjabi ma "guru no akwan". ‘Guru’ no yԑ India som no nyinaa fapem nanso ‘Sikhism’ mu no, ayԑ ade titire a ԑyԑ ‘Sikh’ gyedie nnyinasoɔ.
eng_text: Sikhs call their religion Gurmat, which is Punjabi for "way of the guru". The guru is a fundamental aspect of all Indian religions but in Sikhism has taken on an importance that forms the core of Sikh beliefs.

text: Guru Nanak (1469–1539) na ɔtee saa som yi wɔ ‘15th mfeɛ ɔha a ɛtɔ so no mu. Ɔno akyi no, ‘guru’ ahodoɔ nkron na aba.
eng_text: The religion was founded in the 15th century by Guru Nanak (1469–1539). There followed in succession a further nine gurus.

text: Nanso Ayԑwohomumu 1956 mu no, basabasayԑ a ԑmaa ne ho so wɔ Poland sɔɔ Krushchev bɔhyԑ no hwԑeԑ, wɔ berԑ a na adwumayԑfoɔ a wɔreyԑ ɔyԑkyerԑ fa aduane a ԑnni hɔ ne wɔn akatua a wɔate so no danee ɔyԑkyerԑ a na ԑtia ‘Communism’ no mu.
eng_text: However, in June 1956, Krushchev's promises were put to the test when riots in Poland, where workers were protesting against food shortages and wage cuts, turned into a general protest against Communism.

text: Ɛwom sԑ awieeԑ no Krushchev maa nkurɔfoɔ kɔsɔɔ ano deԑ nanso ɔmaa kwan maa nneԑma no bi yԑԑ adwuma sane tee aseԑ sԑ ɔde Wladyslaw Gomulka a na wagye din no bԑyԑ mansoafoɔ.
eng_text: Although in the end, Krushchev sent in tanks to restore order, he did give way to some economic demands and agreed to appoint the popular Wladyslaw Gomulka as the new prime minister.

text: Na ‘Indus Valley Anibue’ no yԑ ‘Bronze Age anibue’ wɔ ‘northwest Indian’ mpɔtam hɔ a na seesei Pakistan ԑne mantam bi wɔ ‘northwest India’ ԑne ‘northeast Afghanistan’ ka ho.
eng_text: The Indus Valley Civilization was a Bronze Age civilisation in the northwest Indian subcontinent encompassing most of modern-day Pakistan and some regions in northwest India and northeast Afghanistan.

text: Anibue no nyaa nkɔsoɔ wɔ ‘Indus River’ asase a ԑwɔ ne nkyԑn no so nti na edin no da so no.
eng_text: The civilisation flourished in the basins of the Indus River wherefore it derives its name.

text: Animdefo bi kyerԑ sԑ ԑnam sԑ na anibue no wɔ asase a ԑwɔ seesei asuo a awe ‘Sarasvati’ no nti ԑsԑ sԑ ne din yԑ ‘Indus-Sarasvati Anibue’, a ebinom nso frԑ no ‘Harappan Anibue’ ԑnam Harappa nti, beaeԑ a ԑdii kan wɔ 1920s no mu.
eng_text: Although some scholars speculate that since the civilisation also existed in the basins of the now dried up Sarasvati River, it should be aptly called the Indus-Sarasvati Civilization, while some call it the Harappan Civilization after Harappa, the first of its sites to be excavated in the 1920s.

text: Sԑdeԑ na Roman empire no yԑ ‘militaristic’ si teԑ no na ԑmaa nnuroyԑ tuu mpɔn.
eng_text: The militaristic nature of the Roman empire aided in the development of medical advances.

text: Emperor Augustus hyԑԑ aseԑ faa adɔkotafoɔ maa ɔyԑԑ ‘Roman Medical Corps’ a ԑdi kan no sԑdeԑ wɔde bԑyԑ adwuma ɔko akyi.
eng_text: Doctors began to be recruited by Emperor Augustus and even formed the first Roman Medical Corps for use in the aftermath of battles.

text: Na ‘Surgeons’ no wɔ nimdeԑ fa ‘sedatives’ ahodoɔ ho a ‘morphine ԑfiri poppy aba mu ԑne scopolamine a ԑfiri herbane aba mu’ ka ho.
eng_text: Surgeons had knowledge of various sedatives including morphine from extracts of poppy seeds and scopolamine from herbane seeds.

text: Na wɔahunu sԑdeԑ wɔsi yi honam akwaa bi firi hɔ na amma deԑ wapira no annya ‘gangrene’ ԑne ‘tourniquets’ ԑnna ‘arterial clamps’ sԑdeԑ ԑbԑma mogya adi aforosane.
eng_text: They became proficient at amputation to save patients from gangrene as well as tourniquets and arterial clamps to stem blood flow.

text: Mfeɛ ɔha a ɛtɔ so bebree akyi no, Roman empire no nyaa nimdeԑ pii wɔ nnuroyԑ ne apomuden mu a ԑno ne ԑnnԑ nimdeԑ no nnyinasoɔ.
eng_text: Over multiple centuries, the Roman empire led to great gains in the field of medicine and formed much of the knowledge we know today.

text: ‘Pureland origami’ yԑ ‘origami’ ԑma wotumi yԑ ‘fold’ baako pԑ wɔ berԑ bi mu, na wɔmma ‘folds’ a ne yԑ yԑ den te sԑ ‘reverse folds’ ho kwan ԑnna ‘folds’ no nyinaa wɔ baabi pɔtee a wɔwɔ.
eng_text: Pureland origami is origami with the restriction that only one fold may be done at a time, more complex folds like reverse folds are not allowed, and all folds have straightforward locations.

text: John Smith na ɔyԑԑ no wɔ ‘1970s’ no mu de boaa wɔn a wɔnkwadaree ‘fold’ no yԑ mu anaa wɔnni ‘motor skills’ no pii.
eng_text: It was developed by John Smith in the 1970s to help inexperienced folders or those with limited motor skills.

text: Nkwadaa hunu abusua a wɔbɔ ԑne nneԑma a ԑwɔ abusua no ho ntԑm, saa nneԑma yi nso nya nsunsuansoɔ wɔ suban so.
eng_text: Children develop an awareness of race and racial stereotypes quite young and these racial stereotypes affect behavior.

text: Nhwԑsoɔ ne sԑ, nkwadaa a wɔhu wɔn abusua sԑ ԑsua na wɔnyԑ adeԑ wɔ sukuu mu no nso nyԑ adeԑ wɔ sukuu mu berԑ a wɔbԑhu sԑ saa adeԑ no bata n’abusua ho no.
eng_text: For instance, children who identify with a racial minority that is stereotyped as not doing well in school tend to not do well in school once they learn about the stereotype associated with their race.

text: Wɔ United States no, websaet a nkrɔfo kɔ hɔ paa a ɛto so mmiensa yɛ MySpaɔe. Na seiseiaa no, nkrɔfo a wɔn ho nsɛm wɔ hɔ no yɛ 54 million.
eng_text: MySpace is the third most popular website used in the United States and has 54 million profiles currently.

text: Nkrɔfo pii kɔ saa wɛbsaet ahorow yi hɔ, ne titirw adesuafo.
eng_text: These websites have gotten a lot of attention, especially in the education setting.

text: Saa websaet ahorow yi wɔ nneɛma pii a ɛyɛ wɔ ho. Ebi ne sɛ, ɛnyɛ den koraa sɛ wobɛbue klass kraatafa a nneɛma a ɛwɔ hɔ no bi ne blɔgs, sini ahorow, mfoni ahorow ne nkekaho ahorow.
eng_text: There are positive aspects to these websites, which include, being able to easily setup a class page which can include blogs, videos, photos, and other features.

text: Websaet address biako pɛ no bɛtumi de wo akɔ saa kraatafa no so. ɛyi ma no yɛ mmrɛw ma asukuufo a wɔbrɛ sɛ wɔbɛkae na watypo wɔ kiibɔd so anaa wɔɔspɛɛle no.
eng_text: This page can easily be accessed by providing just one web address, which makes it easy to remember and easy to type in for students who may have trouble using the keyboard or with spelling.

text: Wobetumi asesa no na ayɛ mmrɛw sɛ wobɛkenkan, na kɔla no nso wobɛtumi ayɛ no gɔɔn ana ketewaa bi.
eng_text: It can be customized to make it easy to read and also with as much or little color as desired.

text: Attention Deficit Disorder "yԑ adwene mu haw a deԑ ԑkyerԑ no ase ne ‘wobԑyԑ biribi a wonnwene ho’, ‘sԑ wode w’adwene bԑsi deԑ ԑnhia so, ԑne ‘sԑ wobԑpere wɔ biribi ho, anaa wobԑnya ahoɔden ama aboro so".
eng_text: Attention Deficit Disorder "is a neurological syndrome whose classic defining triad of symptoms including impulsivity, distractibility, and hyperactivity or excess energy".

text: Ɛnyԑadesua dԑmdie na mmom ԑyԑ adesua haw; ԑyԑ "nkadwaa ɔha mu abupԑn 3 kɔsi 5, ebia ԑbԑyԑ Amerika nkwadaa ɔpepem mmienu".
eng_text: It is not a learning disability, it is a learning disorder; it "affects 3 to 5 percent of all children, perhaps as many as 2 million American children".

text: Nkwadaa a wɔwɔ ADD ntumi mfa wɔn adwene nsi nneԑma bi te sԑ sukuu dwumadie so, nanso wɔbԑtumi de wɔn adwene akɔ biribi a wɔpԑ ne yԑ so te sԑ wɔrehwԑ cartoons a wɔn ani gye ho anaa wɔretwerԑ ɔkasamu a agyinahyԑdeԑ nni mu.
eng_text: Children with ADD have a hard time focusing on things like school work, but they can concentrate on things they enjoy doing like playing games or watching their favorite cartoons or writing sentences without punctuation.

text: Saa nkwadaa yi taa nya asԑm ԑfiri sԑ "wɔda suban a ԑnyԑ adi, taa ne afoforɔ ko, sɔre tia mpaninnie" sԑdeԑ ԑbԑma wɔn adwene no ayԑ adwuma ԑfiri sԑ kwan a wɔn adwene no yԑ adwuma no yԑ soronko.
eng_text: These children tend to get into a lot of trouble, because they "engage in risky behaviors, get into fights, and challenge authority" in order to stimulate their brain, since their brain can not be stimulated by normal methods.

text: ADD toto ayɔnkofa a wɔne wɔn mfԑfoɔ wɔ ntam ԑfiri sԑ nkwadaa foforɔ ntumi nte deԑ nti a wɔda saa suban no adi anaa deԑ nti a ‘wɔbobɔ atwerԑdeԑ a ԑwɔ asԑmfua no sԑdeԑ wɔyԑ no no, anaa wɔn adwene mu mueeԑ.
eng_text: ADD affects relationships with other peers because other children can not understand why they act the way that they do or why they spell they way they do or that their maturity level is different.

text: Sԑdeԑ tumi a nnipa fa so nya nimdeԑ sane sua adeԑ no sesaeԑ sԑdeԑ yԑaka wɔ soro hɔ no, mprԑ dodoɔ a obi nya nimdeԑ no nso sesaeԑ.
eng_text: As the ability to obtain knowledge and to learn changed in such a way as mentioned above the base rate at which knowledge was obtained changed.

text: Kwan a wɔfa so nya nimdeԑ bi no yԑ soronko. Na kwan a wɔfa so kaekae nneԑma no nyԑ ankorԑankorԑ deԑ bio na mmom sԑ wobԑkae abasԑm no na na wɔhwԑ.
eng_text: The approach to obtaining information was different. No longer did pressure reside within individual recall, but the ability to recall text became more of a focus.

text: Deԑ ԑteԑ ne sԑ, ‘Renaissance’ yԑԑ nsesaeԑ mapa wɔ kwan a yԑfa so sua adeԑ ԑne kwan a yԑfa so de nimdeԑ ma mu.
eng_text: In essence, the Renaissance made a significant change in the approach to learning and the dissemination of knowledge.

text: Na ‘akaatia’ no mfa wɔn nsa nnante bio anaa mfa nkuta adeԑ anaa mfa nto wɔn ho mfa nnua ntam te sԑ wɔn nsԑsoɔ asoroboa nkaeԑ no.
eng_text: Unlike other primates, hominids no longer use their hands in locomotion or bearing weight or swinging through the trees.

text: Akaatia nsa ne ne nan nyinaa kԑseԑ ne ne tenten yԑ pԑ, ԑkyerԑ nsa no dwumadie sԑ ɔnante ne nan so a.
eng_text: The chimpanzee's hand and foot are similar in size and length, reflecting the hand's use for bearing weight in knuckle walking.

text: Nnipa nsa yԑ tia sene ne nan, ԑmu nkasԑԑ no tene.
eng_text: The human hand is shorter than the foot, with straighter phalanges.

text: Nkasԑԑ a adi mfeԑ ɔpepem mmienu kɔsi ɔpepem mmiԑnsa no daa no adi maa yԑhunuu sԑ nsa dwumadie ne adeԑ mu sosɔ na mmom ԑnyԑ nanteԑ.
eng_text: Fossil hand bones two million to three million years old reveal this shift in specialization of the hand from locomotion to manipulation.

text: Ebinom gye di sԑ wobԑso daeԑ bebree wɔ berԑ a w’ani wɔ wo ho so na wonim sԑ woreso daeԑ no yԑ ahomete.
eng_text: Some people believe that experiencing many artificially induced lucid dreams often enough can be very exhausting.

text: Deԑ nti a saa adeԑ yi ne ‘lucid dreams’ no a ԑretrԑ wɔ berԑ yi mu wɔ ‘REM states’ no mu no.
eng_text: The main reason for this phenomenon is the result of the lucid dreams expanding the length of time between REM states.

text: Sԑ wonya ‘REMs’ kakra bi anadwo baako biara a, saa berԑ a wobԑda pa ara ama wo nnipadua no agye n’ahome no ntaa nsi mma nyԑ ɔhaw.
eng_text: With fewer REMs per night, this state in which you experience actual sleep and your body recovers becomes infrequent enough to become a problem.

text: Wei yԑ ahomete te sԑ deԑ ԑsԑ sԑ wosɔre simma aduonu anaa aduasa biara hwԑ TV no.
eng_text: This is just as exhausting as if you were to wake up every twenty or thirty minutes and watch TV.

text: Ɛso nsunsuansoɔ no gyina sԑdeԑ w’adwene no bԑyԑ saa daeԑ yi bi anadwo biara.
eng_text: The effect is dependent on how often your brain attempts to lucidly dream per night.

text: Efiti mfiase no ara na nneɛma ankɔ yiye mma Italifo no wɔ North Afrika. Italifo hyɛɛ ɔsatu ase June 10,1940. Saa naawɔtwe no ara na na Britainfo asraafo kuo 11th Hussars ako agye Capuzzo Aban wɔ Libia afa.
eng_text: Things did not go well for the Italians in North Africa almost from the start. Within a week of Italy's declaration of war on June 10, 1940, the British 11th Hussars had seized Fort Capuzzo in Libya.

text: Britainfo no kɔtɛw Bardia apueifam na wɔkyeree Italifo no asraafo mfiriyɛfo panyin a na ɔtɔ so du, Ɔsahene Lastuɔɔi.
eng_text: In an ambush east of Bardia, the British captured the Italian Tenth Army's Engineer-in-Chief, General Lastucci.

text: Wɔ Ayɛwohomumɔ 28 so no, Marshal Italo Balbo, Libia Amrado-Sahene ne nea na ɛda adi pefee sɛ obedi adeɛ, Mussolini, wui bere a na wɔn wimhyɛn no resi wɔ Tobruk. Wɔn asraafo tuo na ekum wɔn.
eng_text: On June 28, Marshal Italo Balbo, the Governor-General of Libya and apparent heir to Mussolini, was killed by friendly fire while landing in Tobruk.

text: Ɛnnɛyi agodie a wɔfrɛ no "fencing" no wɔ afa ahodoɔ bebree, efi adesuafoɔ a wɔwɔ sukuupɔn mu kosi wɔn a wɔreyɛ adwuma ne Olympic akansie mu.
eng_text: The modern sport of fencing is played at many levels, from students learning at a university to professional and Olympic competition.

text: Wɔtaa di saa agodie yi wɔ ntɔkwa kwan so, ɔgodifoɔ baako reko tia ne yɔnko.
eng_text: The sport is primarily played in a duel format, one fencer dueling another.

text: Golf yɛ agodie bi a agodifoɔ no de mporibaa bɔ bɔɔlo no hyɛ tokuro mu.
eng_text: Golf is a game in which players use clubs to hit balls into holes.

text: Wɔde ntokuro dunwɔtwe na edi agurɔ yei mpɛn pii, na agodifoɔ no firi aseɛ wɔ tokuro a edi kan wɔ agodibeaeɛ hɔ na wowie wɔ deɛ ɛtɔ soɔ dunwɔtwe no so.
eng_text: Eighteen holes are played during a regular round, with players usually starting on the first hole on the course and finishing on the eighteenth.

text: Ɔgodifoɔ a obewie agorɔ no berɛ a ɔto n'aporibaa no mpɛn kakraa bi no na odi nkonim.
eng_text: The player who takes the fewest strokes, or swings of the club, to complete the course wins.

text: Wodi saa agorɔ yei wɔ ɛserɛsoɔ, na wotwa ɛserɛ a etwa tokuro no ho ahyia no ma ɛyɛ tiatiaa sene deɛ aka no na wɔfrɛ no ahabammono.
eng_text: The game is played on grass, and the grass around the hole is mown shorter and called the green.

text: Ɛbɛyɛ sɛ nsrahwɛ a agye din paa ne deɛ ɛfa akwantuo ho a nnipa anigye ho: Anigyediɛ nsrahwɛ.
eng_text: Perhaps the most common type of tourism is what most people associate with traveling: Recreation tourism.

text: Yei ne berɛ a nkurɔfoɔ kɔ mmeaeɛ a ɛda nso wɔ wɔn daa daa asetena mu de home na wɔde gye wɔn ani.
eng_text: This is when people go to a place that is very different from their regular day-to-day life to relax and have fun.

text: Mpoano, agodi beaeɛ ne beaeɛ a wosi ntomadan da mu yɛ beaeɛ a anigyediɛ nsrahwɛfoɔ tae kɔ.
eng_text: Beaches, theme parks and camp grounds are often the most common places frequented by recreational tourists.

text: Sɛ onii a ɔrekɔ beaeɛ bi no botaeɛ ne sɛ obesua beaeɛ no abakɔsɛm ne wɔn amammerɛ a, ende na wɔfrɛ saa nsrahwɛ yei sɛ amammerɛ nsrahwɛ.
eng_text: If the objective of one’s visit to a particular place is to get to know its history and culture then this type of tourism is known as cultural tourism.

text: Nsrahwɛfoɔ tumi kɔsra mmeaeɛ a agye din ahodoɔ wɔ kuro pɔtee bi mu anaasɛ wɔpaw sɛ wɔde wɔn adwene besi beaeɛ baako pɛ soɔ.
eng_text: Tourists may visit different landmarks of a particular country or they may simply opt to focus on just one area.

text: Berɛ a wohunuu deɛ ɛrekɔ soɔ no, atukɔtenafoɔ no ma wɔde asraafoɔ no bi bɛkaa wɔn ho.
eng_text: The Colonists, seeing this activity, had also called for reinforcements.

text: Asraafoɔ a wɔbɛkaa wɔn a wodi anim no ho no ne 1st ne 3rd Hampshire asraafoɔ kuo a wɔyɛ mmarima 200, a na wɔhyɛ Colonel John Stark ne James Reed (a wɔbɛyɛɛ asahene) aseɛ.
eng_text: Troops reinforcing the forward positions included the 1st and 3rd New Hampshire regiments of 200 men, under Colonels John Stark and James Reed (both later became generals).

text: Stark mmarima no gyinaa beaeɛ a atukɔtenafoɔ no wↄ wↄn atifi fam wↄ ɛban no ho.
eng_text: Stark's men took positions along the fence on the north end of the Colonist's position.

text: Berɛ a asorɔkye no baa fam no, ɛmaa kwan bɛdaa Mystic asubɔtene no ho wɔ asase a na nsuo atwa ho ahyia ne fa bi atifiapueeɛ mantam hɔ. Ntɛm ara na wɔde aboɔ yɛɛ ban tiatia bi trɛɛ wɔn hyeɛ mu kosii mpoano ketewa bi wɔ nsuo no ano atifi fam.
eng_text: When low tide opened a gap along the Mystic River along the northeast of the peninsula, they quickly extended the fence with a short stone wall to the north ending at the water's edge on a small beach.

text: Gridley ne Stark de dua a ne tenten bɛyɛ anammɔn 100 (30 m) sii ɛban no anim na ɔhyɛe sɛ obiara ntu tuo kosi sɛ wobewie deɛ ɛsɛ sɛ wɔyɛ.
eng_text: Gridley or Stark placed a stake about 100 feet (30 m) in front of the fence and ordered that no one fire until the regulars passed it.

text: Na Amerikafoɔ no tirimupɔ ne sɛ wɔbɛto ahyɛ wɔn so wɔ akwan ahodoɔ mmieɛnsa soɔ denam toto a wɔbɛtoto wɔn nneɛma yie.
eng_text: The American plan relied on launching coordinated attacks from three different directions.

text: Ɔsahene John Cadwalder bɛto ahyɛ Britainfoɔ asraafoɔ a wɔrebɔ ban wɔ Bordentown de atwe wɔn adwene firi hɔ, sɛdeɛ wobetumi asi mmoa biara a ɛbɛba ho kwan.
eng_text: General John Cadwalder would launch a diversionary attack against the British garrison at Bordentown, in order to block off any reinforcements.

text: Ɔsahene James Ewing de asraafoɔ 700 betwa esubontene no wɔ Trenton Ferry, na wɔde wɔn nsa bɛto nsamsoɔ a ɛwɔ nsuka no so na woasi atamfoɔ no asraafoɔ no kwan na woantumi annwane.
eng_text: General James Ewing would take 700 militia across the river at Trenton Ferry, seize the bridge over the Assunpink Creek and prevent any enemy troops from escaping.

text: Asraafoɔ dɔm a wobedi ako no ankasa betwa asubontene no akwansini nkron wɔ Trenton atifi fam, na wɔbɛkyɛ wɔn mu ekuo mmienu, kuo baako hyɛ Greene aseɛ na baako nso hyɛ Sullivan aseɛ, sɛdeɛ wɔbɛto ahyɛ wɔn so ansa na ahemadakye aduru.
eng_text: The main assault force of 2,400 men would cross the river nine miles north of Trenton, and then split into two groups, one under Greene and one under Sullivan, in order to launch a pre-dawn attack.

text: Esiane sɛ wɔasesa mmirikatuo no firi anan mu nkyekyemu baako kɔ ɛfa no nti, ama ahohyɛsoɔ hu abehia sene ahoɔhare.
eng_text: With the change from the quarter to the half mile run, speed becomes of much less importance and endurance becomes an absolute necessity.

text: Ne saa nti ɛsɛ sɛ obi a wakwadare mmirika a wotu no akwansini fa no, tumi de sima mmienu so nkonim, ɛsɛ sɛ ne ho yɛ hare deɛ nanso ɛsɛ sɛ otumi hyɛ ne ho so wɔ akwansideɛ ahodoɔ a obehyia no mu.
eng_text: Of course a first-class half-miler, a man who can beat two minutes, must be possessed of a fair amount of speed, but endurance must be cultivated at all hazards.

text: Ansa na mmirikatuo berɛ no bɛhyɛ aseɛ no, nsiesie pa a wobetumi ayɛ ne sɛ wode wo ho bɛhyɛ mmirika a wotu fa kuro mu awɔbrɛ mu na wode apɔmutenetene a ɛyɛ ma nipadua ne fa ewɔ soro no ka ho.
eng_text: Some cross country running during the winter, combined with gymnasium work for the upper part of the body, is the best preparation for the running season.

text: Nnuane pa a yedie nkoa rentumi mma yɛnkɔ kan wɔ akansie mu, nanso ebetumi aboa akansifoɔ a wɔyɛ afoforɔ no apɔmuden.
eng_text: Proper nutritional practices alone cannot generate elite performances, but they can significantly affect young athletes' overall wellness.

text: Akwahosan a edi mu, nsuo a yɛtaa nom ne te a yɛbɛte sɛdeɛ nnuru a yɛde si nnuane anan mu no yɛ adwuma fa no bɛboa mmirikatufoɔ ma wɔakɔ wɔn anim na wɔn ani agye agodie no ho.
eng_text: Maintaining a healthy energy balance, practicing effective hydration habits, and understanding the various aspects of supplementation practices can help athletes improve their performance and increase their enjoyment of the sport.

text: Amirikatuo a ɛnyɛ tenten pii yɛ akansie a ne boɔ nhyɛda nyɛ den; nanso, nkorɔfoɔ wɔ adwene bi wɔ nneɛma kakra a ehia na ama wɔatumi asi akan no.
eng_text: Middle distance running is a relatively inexpensive sport; however, there are many misconceptions regarding the few pieces of equipment required to participate.

text: Wobetumi atɔ ɛho akadeɛ sɛdeɛ wo berɛ a wohia, nanso ɛrenhyɛda nya nsunsuansoɔ biara wɔ deɛ wobɛyɛ no so.
eng_text: Products can be purchased as needed, but most will have little or no real impact on performance.

text: Agodifoɔ no bɛte nka sɛ wohia akadeɛ bi ɛberɛ a saa ade korɔ no mfa mfasoɔ papa biara mmrɛ no.
eng_text: Athletes may feel that they prefer a product even when it provides no real benefits.

text: Yebetumi aka sɛ atom yɛ nneɛma a eka bom yɛ matter no deɛ edi mu akotene paa.
eng_text: The atom can be considered to be one of the fundamental building blocks of all matter.

text: Sɛdeɛ Bohr nhwɛsoɔ a wɔatwa no tia no kyerɛ no, ɛyɛ adeɛ a ɛyɛ nwonworann paa, a electron no redi nucleus no a ɛwɔ ne mfinfini no ho kyinhyia te sɛ sɛdeɛ okyinsoroma twa owia no ho hyia no. Hwɛ mfonini 1.1.
eng_text: Its a very complex entity which consists, according to a simplified Bohr model, of a central nucleus orbited by electrons, somewhat similar to planets orbiting the sun - see Figure 1.1.

text: Nneɛma nketenkete mmienu ɛna ɛbom yɛ nucleus no - neutrons ne protons.
eng_text: The nucleus consists of two particles - neutrons and protons.

text: Proton no wɔ anyinam tumi a ɛyɛ positive na neutron no nni tumi biara. Electron no wɔ anyinam tumi a ɛyɛ negative.
eng_text: Protons have a positive electric charge while neutrons have no charge. The electrons have a negative electric charge.

text: Ansa na wobɛhwɛ opirafo no, ɛsɛ sɛ wodi kan hwɛ beaeɛ a ɔda no yie na woamfa wo ho anto asiane mu.
eng_text: To Check the victim, you must first survey the scene to ensure your safety.

text: Bere a worebɛn no no, ɛsɛ sɛ wohwɛ beaeɛ a opirafo no da ne biribiara a ebetumi ayɛ asiane nso.
eng_text: You need to notice the victim's position as you approach him or her and any automatic red flags.

text: Sɛ wo a worekɔboa opirafo no nso pira a, eyi bɛma tebea no asɛe koraa.
eng_text: If you get hurt trying to help, you may only serve to make matters worse.

text: Nhwehwɛmu ama ada edi sɛ berɛ a obi abotow, ehu aka no na ɔma adeɛ yɛ hu sene sɛdeɛ ɛteɛ no na ɛde ɛyeaa ne mmerɛwyɛ ba wɔn a wɔn akyi ase yɛ wɔn ya no mu.
eng_text: The study found that depression, fear and catastrophising mediated the relationship between pain and disability in lower back pain sufferers.

text: Nsunsuansoɔ a wɔn a wɔma adeɛ yɛ hu sene sɛdeɛ ɛteɛ no nya no na ɛma wɔhyehyɛɛ nnawɔtwe biara PA nhyiamu no na ɛnyɛ abotow ne ehu ntira.
eng_text: Only the effects of catastrophizing, not depression and fear was conditional of regular weekly structured PA sessions.

text: Sɛ yɛreka adwene pa a wonni wɔ ɛyeaa ho a ɛne sɛ wobehu nsonsonoe a eda ɛyeaa koankorɔ ne honam yeaa esaine ahokeka no a, wɔn a wɔyɛ adwuma berɛ nyinaa no‪ behia mmoa yie.
eng_text: Those participating in regular activity required more support in terms of negative perception of pain distinguishing the differences of chronic pain and discomfort feel from normal physical movement.

text: Hunu a yehunu adeɛ no gyina yɛn akwaa a ɛma yehunu adeɛ no anaa aniwa no so.
eng_text: Vision, or the ability to see depends on visual system sensory organs or eyes.

text: Nneɛma ahodoɔ a ɛda nsow na wɔde ayɛ aniwa no, na emu ntiaseɛ yɛtumi yɛ nworanworan denam nkwaboa no ahiadeɛ so.
eng_text: There are many different constructions of eyes, ranging in complexity depending on the requirements of the organism.

text: Sɛdeɛ wɔyɛɛ emu biara ɛnna ahoɔden soronko ɛwɔ, ehu han ahodoɔ ntɛm na ne namyɛ nso nyɛ pɛ. Afei nso, ɛsono deɛ ebehunu biara ne sɛdeɛ ɛbɛte aseɛ na sɛ ɛbɛyɛ adwuma yie a, ehia nɔma ahodoɔ.
eng_text: The different constructions have different capabilities, are sensitive to different wave-lengths and have differing degrees of acuity, also they require different processing to make sense of the input and different numbers to work optimally.

text: Population yɛ abɔdeɛ no dodoɔ a wɔn nnyinaa te asaase ne fa pɔtee bi so.
eng_text: A population is the collection of organisms of a particular species within a given geographic area.

text: Sɛ akorankoro nnyinaa a wɔte asaase no beae pɔtee bi no di nsɛ paa wɔ nipadua no su ahodoɔ a ani tumi hu ho a, wɔfrɛ wɔn abɔdeɛ a wɔn suban yɛ baako.
eng_text: When all individuals in a population are identical with regard to a particular phenotypic trait they are known as monomorphic.

text: Sɛ akorankoro biara da su pɔtee bi adi akwan ahodoɔ ahodoɔ so a, wɔfrɛ wɔn abɔde a wɔn suban gu ahodoɔ.
eng_text: When the individuals show several variants of a particular trait they are polymorphic.

text: Ntatea bom sɛ ekuo nante na wɔhome wɔ akwan ahorow pii so.
eng_text: Army ant colonies march and nest in different phases as well.

text: Sɛ a wɔretwa kwan no, ntatea yi nante anwumerɛ na wɔhome bereɛ a ade akye.
eng_text: In the nomadic phase, army ants march at night and stop to camp during the day.

text: Kuo no fi ase twa kwan berɛ a aduane a ɛwɔ hɔ no so ateɛ. Eduru saa berɛ yi a, da biara kuo no yɛ esie ahodoɔ na ɛnkyɛ na wɔasesa no.
eng_text: The colony begins a nomadic phase when available food has decreased. During this phase, the colony makes temporary nests that are changed everyday.

text: Saa akwantwa anaa nanteɛ yi di bɛyɛ nna 17 berɛ biara.
eng_text: Each of these nomadic rampages or marches lasts for approximately 17 days.

text: Dɛn ne nkwammoaa? Asɛmfua nkwammoaa firi Latin asɛmfua "cella", a deɛ ɛkyerɛ ne "ɔdan ketewa bi", na wodii kan de saa asɛmfua yi dii dwuma berɛ a na obi a ɔhwɛ nneɛma nketenkete a aniwa ntumi nhnuu mu no rehwɛ sɛdeɛ wɔahyehyɛ nsatire no mu no.
eng_text: What is a cell? The word cell comes from the Latin word "cella", meaning "small room", and it was first coined by a microscopist observing the structure of cork.

text: Nkwammoaa no ne ade titiriw a abɔdeɛ a nkwa wɔ mu nkwa nyinaa gyina so, na abɔdeɛ nyinaa wɔ nkwammoaa yi baako anaa deɛ ɛboro saa.
eng_text: The cell is the basic unit of all living things, and all organisms are composed of one or more cells.

text: Nkwammoa ho hia paa titire berɛ a yeresua nkwa ho adeɛ no, kyerɛ sɛ, wɔtaa frɛ wɔn "ntayaa a wɔde hyehyɛɛ nkwa".
eng_text: Cells are so basic and critical to the study of life, in fact, that they are often referred to as "the building blocks of life".

text: Amemene no hwɛ ma biribiara kɔ so pɛpɛɛpɛ wɔ nipadua no mu. Na ɛyɛ saa berɛ a ɛde anyinam nketenkete fa ntini no mu na ama mogya adi aforosiane a biribiara nsi ne kwan wɔ nipadua no mu.
eng_text: The Nervous System maintains homeostasis by sending nerve impulses through out the body to keep the flow of blood going as well as undisturbed.

text: Anyinam nketenkete a ɛfa ntini no mu no tumi kɔ ntɛm paa wɔ nipadua no mu na eyi bɔ nipadua no ho ban fi ɛyea biara a ɛbɛsɔre ho.
eng_text: These nerve impulses can be sent so quickly throughout the body which helps keep the body safe from any potential threat.

text: Sɛ wode atɔyerɛnkyɛm ahodoɔ toto ho a, mframa gyampantrudu si wɔ beaeɛ ketewa bi nanso ɛsɛe biribiara a ɛda ne kwan mu no.
eng_text: Tornadoes strike a small area compared to other violent storms, but they can destroy everything in their path.

text: Mframa gyampantrudu tutu nnua a esisi hɔ, ɛwae nnua a ɛbobɔ dan so, na ɛma kaa so to kɔ wiem. Mframa gyampantrudu a ano yɛ den paa no mu ɔha mu nkyem mmienu pɛ tumi di boro nnɔnhwere mmiɛnsa.
eng_text: Tornadoes uproot trees, rip boards from buildings, and fling cars up into the sky. The most violent two percent of tornadoes last more than three hours.

text: Wɔ ahum akɛse paa mu no, mframa no anoɔden no tumi duru 480 km/h (133m/s; 300 mph).
eng_text: These monster storms have winds up to 480 km/h (133 m/s; 300 mph).

text: Nnipa akɔso ayɛ ahwehwɛniwa na aboa ma wɔahu nneɛma nketenkete mfeɛ mpempem pii nie.
eng_text: Humans have been making and using lenses for magnification for thousands and thousands of years.

text: Nanso, wodii kan yɛɛ ahwehwɛniwa a wɔde hwɛ wiem ankasa wɔ Europa wɔ afeha a ɛtɔ so 16 no awieiɛ no mu hɔ.
eng_text: However, the first true telescopes were made in Europe in the late 16th century.

text: Wɔde ahwehwɛniwa ahodoɔ mmienu na ɛbom yɛ saa ahwehwɛniwa a wɔde hwɛ wiem no na etumi ama nneɛma a ɛwowɔ akyire no abɛn na ayɛ akɛseɛ nso.
eng_text: These telescopes used a combination of two lenses to make distant objects appear both nearer and larger.

text: Adwuma a yɛyɛ no bɛnkorɔ no kyerɛ sɛ, sɛ nnipa dodoɔ no ara nya so mfasoɔ a wobetumi anya pii berɛ tiawa mu sɛ wɔyɛ pɛsɛmenkomenya a. Ɛno nti adufudepɛ ne pɛsɛmenkomenya ne yɛn bɛtena daa.
eng_text: Greed and selfishness will always be with us and it is the nature of cooperation that when the majority benefit there will always be more to gain in the short term by acting selfishly

text: Yɛhwɛ kwan sɛ, nnipa dodoɔ no ara behunu sɛ deɛ ɛbɛboa ne sɛ wɔne afoforɔ bɛbom ayɛ adwuma.
eng_text: Hopefully, most people will realise that their long term best option is to work together with others.

text: Nnipa pii daeɛ so ne sɛ wobetumi atukwan akɔhwɛ nsoroma foforɔ ne wiase foforɔ, ebinom dwennwen dea ɛwɔ hɔ ho ebinom gye di sɛ amanfrafoɔ anaa adeɛ foforɔ a nkwa wɔ mu na ɛwɔ okyinsoroma foforɔ bi so.
eng_text: Many people dream of the day when humans can travel to another star and explore other worlds, some people wonder what's out there some belive that aliens or other life may live on another plant.

text: Nanso, sɛ wei bɛsi mpo a ɛbɛkyɛ paa ansa na esi. Nsoroma no ntɛm atete ma akwansin ɔpepemhuhaa na ɛda nsoroma a wɔye "efipamfoɔ" ntam.
eng_text: But, if this ever does happen probably won't happen for a very long time. The stars are so spread out that there are trillions of miles between stars that are "neighbors".

text: Ebia dakorɔ, wo nanankansewanom begyina amanfrafoɔ wiase bi so na wɔbɛ dwennwene wɔn nananom ho?
eng_text: Maybe one day, your great grandchildren will be standing atop an alien world wondering about their ancient ancestors?

text: Nkwanmoa pii na ɛwɔ mmoa mu. Wɔdi biribiara na ɛyam no wɔ nipadua no mu. Mmoa pii tumi keka wɔn ho.
eng_text: Animals are made of many cells. They eat things and digest them inside. Most animals can move.

text: Mmoa nkoaa na wɔ wɔ adwene (nanso ɛnyɛ wɔn nyinaa na wɔ wɔ bi; jellyfish, sɛ nhwesoɔ no, enni adwene).
eng_text: Only animals have brains (though not even all animals do; jellyfish, for example, do not have brains).

text: Yehu mmoa wɔ wiase yi mu baabiara. Wotutu fam, wodware wɔ ɛpo mu, na wotu wɔ ewiemu.
eng_text: Animals are found all over the earth. They dig in the ground, swim in the oceans, and fly in the sky.

text: Nkwanmoa yɛ abɔdeɛ (nnoɔma) a nkwa wɔmu fa ketewa bi.
eng_text: A cell is the smallest structural and functional unit of a living (things) organism.

text: Nkwammoa (cells) fi Latin asɛmfua cella mu a ɛkyerɛ ɔdan ketewa.
eng_text: Cell comes from the Latin word cella which means small room.

text: Sɛ wohwɛ nkwammoa wɔ microscope aseɛ a, wobehu sɛ ahinanan anaa kukuruwa na ayɛ no ma.
eng_text: If you look at living things under a microscope, you will see that they are made of small squares or balls.

text: Abɔdeɛ a nkwa wɔmu ho adesuani, Robert Hooke a ofi England, de microscope huu ahinanan nketewa a ɛwɔ cork mu.
eng_text: Robert Hooke, a biologist from England, saw small squares in cork with a microscope.

text: Wɔte sɛ adan. Ɔno ne nipa a odi kan a ohuu nkwanmoa a wɔn awuwu.
eng_text: They looked like rooms. He was the first person to observe dead cells

text: Nnoɔma ne nnoɔma afrafra betumi asesa efiri tebea baako mu akɔ foforɔ mu a ɛnsesa.
eng_text: Elements and compounds can move from one state to another and not change.

text: Nitrogen yɛ ogyamframa a ɛsan tesɛ nitrogen a ɛsen. Ne nsesen mu no emu yɛ duru nanso emu nnoɔma no yɛpɛ.
eng_text: Nitrogen as a gas still has the same properties as liquid nitrogen. The liquid state is denser but the molecules are still the same.

text: Nsuo nso yɛ nhwɛsoɔ foforɔ. Hydrogen atoms ne oxygen atoms na ɛwɔ nsuo mu.
eng_text: Water is another example. The compound water is made up of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

text: Ɛwɔ saa nhyehyɛ no pɛpɛɛpɛ sɛ ɛyɛ ogyamframa, dea ɛsen, anaa nea ɛyɛ den.
eng_text: It has the same molecular structure whether it is a gas, liquid, or solid.

text: Ɛmfa ho sɛ sɛdeɛ ɛte betumi asesa no, n'aduru mu deɛ ɛnsesa.
eng_text: Although its physical state may change, its chemical state remains the same.

text: Mmerɛ yɛ adeɛ a ɛwɔ yɛnkyɛn aberɛ biara, na ɛka deaɛ yɛyɛ biara, nanso yɛntumi nte aseɛ.
eng_text: Time is something that is all around us, and affects everything we do, yet is difficult to understand.

text: Nyamesomfoɔ, nyansapɛfoɔ ne nyansahufoɔ de mfe boro ɔpepem na asua mmerɛ ho adeɛ.
eng_text: Time has been studied by religious, philosophical, and scientific scholars for thousands of years.

text: Yehu sɛ mmerɛ yɛ nnoɔma a esisi mmɔho abakɔsɛm a efi nnɛ berɛ mu de kosi tete berɛ mu.
eng_text: We experience time as a series of events passing from the future through the present to the past.

text: Mmerɛ nso yɛ sɛdeɛ yɛ de nnoɔma a esisi bɛtoto sɛdeɛ ɛkyɛ (tenten) ho.
eng_text: Time is also how we compare the duration (length) of events.

text: Wo ankasa wobetumi asusu sɛdeɛ mmerɛ kɔ sɛ wohwɛ sɛdeɛ nnoɔma pɔtee sisi a. Nnoɔma pɔtee a esisi ntuatua so yɛ nnoɔma a ɛkɔ so sisi bere ne bere mu.
eng_text: You can mark the passing of time yourself by observing the repetition of a cyclical event. A cyclical event is something that happens again and again regularly.

text: Kɔmputa a ɛwɔ hɔ nnɛ no wɔde yɛ sini nketewa ne mfoni ho adwuma.
eng_text: Computers today are used to manipulate pictures and videos.

text: Sinitwa a aba soɔ no wɔde kɔmputa na ɛyɛ, na saa sinitwa a ɛte saa nu woyi no paa wɔ TV so ne sini ahodoɔ mu.
eng_text: Sophisticated animations can be constructed on computers, and this kind of animation is increasingly being used in television and films.

text: Wɔtae de kɔmputa ahodoɔ a aba so no na etwa nnwom na wɔkeka ngyigyeɛ ahodoɔ bɔmu.
eng_text: Music is often recorded using sophisticated computers to process and mix sounds together.

text: Efiti bere tenten wɔ mfe ɔpepem akrɔn ne mfe ɔpepem aduonu bere mu no, na wɔgyedi sɛ nnipa a wɔdii kan tenaa New Zealand yɛ Maorifoɔ, a na nnoma akɛseɛ a wɔferɛ wɔn moas na wɔkyere wɔn sɛ wɔkɔ ahayɔ a.
eng_text: For a long time during the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, it was believed the first inhabitants of New Zealand were the Maori people, who hunted giant birds called moas.

text: Nsɛm no san kyerɛɛ sɛ Maorifoɔ no to fii Polynesia wɔ Great Fleet na wɔ bɛgyee New Zealand fii Moriorifoɔ no nsam, na wɔbɛtee akuafoɔ asafo.
eng_text: The theory then established the idea that the Maori people migrated from Polynesia in a Great Fleet and took New Zealand from the Moriori, establishing an agricultural society.

text: Nanso no, adanseɛ foforɔ kyerɛ sɛ na Moriorifoɔ no yɛ Maori asaase no fa kɛseɛ mu foɔ a wɔfi New Zealand kɔɔ Chathan Nsuopoɔ so, na wɔfii aseɛ yɛɛ wɔn nnoɔma foforɔ, amammerɛ a asomdwo wɔmu.
eng_text: However, new evidence suggests that the Moriori were a group of mainland Maori who migrated from New Zealand to the Chatham Islands, developing their own distinctive, peaceful culture.

text: Na abusuakuo foforɔ bi nso wɔ Chathan nsuopɔ no so wei yɛ Maorifoɔ a wɔtu fii New Zealand.
eng_text: There was also another tribe on the Chatham islands these were Maori who migrated away from New Zealand.

text: Wɔferɛɛ wɔn ho Moriorifoɔ na abenne die kakra wɔ hɔ na ewi aseɛ no, wɔpopaa Moriorifoɔ no fi hɔ.
eng_text: They called themselves the Moriori there were a few skirmishes and in the end, the Moriori were wiped out

text: Ankorɛankorɛ a na wɔka ho bɛyɛ mfenhyia du bi no boaa yɛn ma yɛn ani sɔɔ nea yetumi yɛ ne dea yɛn ani gye ho aberɛ a yɛsusu yɛn akwansideɛ ne mpo nkuguodie ho no.
eng_text: Individuals who had been involved for several decades helped us appreciate our strengths and passions while candidly assessing difficulties and even failures.

text: Aberɛ a yɛɛtie ankorɛankorɛ sɛ wɔka wɔn ho, wɔn abusua, ne wɔn adwumayɛbea ho nsɛm no, yɛbɛnyaa nhumu a edi mu fa tete ho ne nnipa bi a wɔnyaa kuo no ho nneɛma pa ne nneɛma bɔne ho nkɛntɛnsoɔ.
eng_text: While listening to individuals share their individual, family, and organizational stories, we gained valuable insight into the past and some of the personalities who influenced for good or ill the culture of the organization.

text: Aberɛ a wore te obi abakɔsɛm aseɛ no nkyerɛ sɛ wote n'amammerɛ aseɛ, nanso no ɛboa ma wonya baabi a wɔgyina wɔ kuo no mo abakɔsɛm ho adwene.
eng_text: While understanding one’s history does not assume understanding of culture, it does at least help people gain a sense of where they fall within the history of the organization.

text: Aberɛ a wɔ susu wɔn nkunimdie na wɔhu wɔn nkuguodie ho no, ankorɛankorɛ ne kuo no mu foɔ a wɔgusu sua adeɛ no nyinaa behu kuo no so mfasoɔ, kuo no botaeɛ ne deɛ ɛma kuo no kɔ so.
eng_text: While assessing the successes and becoming aware of failures, individuals and the whole of the participating persons discover more deeply the values, mission, and driving forces of the organization.

text: Wɔ saa tebeaɛ wei mu no, kae a wɔ kae adwuma ho suban a esisi atwam ne nkunimdie a ɛde baeɛ no boaa nkuroɔfoɔ ma wɔ buee nsesaeɛ foforɔ ne nkyerɛkyerɛ foforɔ maa kuro no mu asɔre no.
eng_text: In this instance, recalling previous instances of entrepreneurial behavior and resulting successes helped people to be open to new changes and new direction for the local church.

text: Saa nkunimdie ho asɛm wei maa nsakraeɛ ho hu no kɔɔ fam, aberɛ nso a na ɛreda daakye ho nsakraeɛ adi wɔ wɔn mu.
eng_text: Such success stories lessened the fears of change, while creating positive inclinations toward change in the future.

text: Adwenkoro nhwɛsode ye ɔhaw anosɔ kwan a ɛka nsusuii ahorow anaa nimdeɛ ahorow bom de sɔ ɔhaw ano.
eng_text: Convergent thinking patterns are problem solving techniques that unite different ideas or fields to find a solution.

text: Saa adwenpɔ yi botae ye amirika, enidiso, nokwasɛm, bio nso nokwasɛm a wɔbɛhyɛ no nsow, akwan ahorow a wɔbɛsan de adi dwuma bio, ne nsɛm a wɔbɛboaboa ano.
eng_text: The focus of this mindset is speed, logic and accuracy, also identification of facts, reapplying existing techniques, gathering information.

text: Adeɛ a ɛho hia paa fa saa adwenpɔ yi ho ne sɛ: mmuae baako pɛ na ɛwɔ hɔ. Wodwen mmuae mmienu pɛ ho, a ɛne woatwa anaa woaten.
eng_text: The most important factor of this mindset is: there is only one correct answer. You only think of two answers, namely right or wrong.

text: Saa kwan a wɔfa so dwen no hyɛ nyansahu anaa gyinapɛn bi ase.
eng_text: This type of thinking is associated with certain science or standard procedures.

text: Nkrɔfo a wɔwɔ saa adwene no dwen nnidisonnidiso, no wɔtumi kyere ade a ɛyɛ sɔnnahɔ gu wɔn tirim, sɔw ɔhaw ano, na wɔtumi yɛ nyansahu mu nhwehwɛmu ho adwuma.
eng_text: People with this type of thinking have logical thinking, are able to memorize patterns, solve problems and work on scientific tests.

text: Nnipa na ɛyɛ mmoa a wɔwɔ adom akyɛdeɛ a wɔ de hu deɛ afoforɔ dwene.
eng_text: Humans are by far the most talented species in reading the minds of others.

text: Wei kyerɛ sɛ yetumi de yɛn adwene bu deɛ afoforɔ susu ho, deɛ wɔn abɔ wɔ tirimu sɛ wɔbɛyɛ, deɛ wɔgyedi, deɛ wɔnim anaa deɛ wɔpɛ.
eng_text: That means we are able to successfully predict what other humans perceive, intend, believe, know or desire.

text: Deɛ ɛka saa nnoɔma a yɛetumi yi ho no, afoforɔ nsusuyɛ a yɛbɛte aseɛ no ho hia paa. Ɛma yɛn kwan ma yɛtumi di nnoɔma a ɛsisi ma yɛhu a ɛho nteaseɛ yɛ akɛseɛ ho dwuma.
eng_text: Among these abilities, understanding the intention of others is crucial. It allows us to resolve possible ambiguities of physical actions.

text: Sɛ nhwɛsoɔ no, sɛ ɛba sɛ wuhu sɛ obi repae hyɛn bi mfɛnsere a, wobetumi asusu sɛ ɔrebɔ mmɔden awia obi a ɔnnim no hyɛn.
eng_text: For example, if you were to see someone breaking a car window, you would probably assume he was trying to steal a stranger’s car.

text: Wobɛbu no atɛn wɔ ɔkwan foforɔ so sɛ wayera ne hyɛn no nsafoa na ɛyɛ ɔnoa ne hyɛn na ɔrebɔ mɔden sɛ ɔbɛbu awura mu a.
eng_text: He would need to be judged differently if he had lost his car keys and it was his own car that he was trying to break into.

text: MRI gyina abɔdeɛ ho nimdeɛ a wɔferɛ no nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) gyinapɛn so, na Felix Bloch (ɔyɛ adwuma wɔ Stanford University) ne Edward Purcell (ofi Harvard University) na wɔ huu ho adeɛ wɔ 1930s mu.
eng_text: MRI is based on a physics phenomenon called nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), which was discovered in the 1930s by Felix Bloch (working at Stanford University) and Edward Purcell (from Harvard University).

text: Wɔ saa resonance wei mu no, baabi a tweboɔ wɔ ne akasafidie ho mframa ma atoms de akasafidie ho adafitwa sɛnkyerɛne nketenkete ma.
eng_text: In this resonance, magnetic field and radio waves cause atoms to give off tiny radio signals.

text: Wɔ afe 1970 mu no, Raymond Damadian, a ɔyɛ oduruyɛfoɔ ne nhwehwɛmu ho nyansapɛfoɔ, huu nea enti a wɔde tweboɔ ho dede ho mfonini yɛ adwinnade a wɔde yɛ nyarewa mu nhwehwɛmu.
eng_text: In the year 1970, Raymond Damadian, a medical doctor and research scientist, discovered the basis for using magnetic resonance imaging as a tool for medical diagnosis.

text: Mfe anan akyi no wɔde ɛho tumi maeɛ, ɛno na na ɛyɛ wiase nyinaa tumi a edi kan a wɔde maeɛ wɔ MRI adwumayɛ ho.
eng_text: Four years later a patent was granted, which was the world's first patent issued in the field of MRI.

text: Wɔ 1977 mu no, Dr, Damadian wie “whole-body” MRI nhwehwɛmu afidie a edi kan no ho adwumayɛ, na ɔferɛɛ no ”Indomitable”.
eng_text: In 1977, Dr. Damadian completed the construction of the first “whole-body” MRI scanner, which he called the ”Indomitable”.

text: Nkɔmmɔbɔ a ɛnkɔ so wɔ berɛ baako mu no boa yi berɛ ma adwennwene ne sɛdeɛ yɛne afoforɔ di.
eng_text: Asynchronous communication encourages time for reflection and reaction to others.

text: Ɛma kwan ma asuafoɔ tumi yɛ adwuma wɔ wɔn ankasa berɛ mu na wɔn ankasa di berɛ a wɔde yɛ ɔkasa ho nkyerɛkyerɛ.
eng_text: It allows students the ability to work at their own pace and control the pace of instructional information.

text: Deɛ ɛka ho no, anohweteɛ kakra wɔ mmerɛ a yebetumi de ayɛ adwuma no so. (Bremer, 1998)
eng_text: In addition, there are fewer time restrictions with the possibility of flexible working hours. (Bremer, 1998)

text: Wiase ntontan kɛseɛ a yɛde yɛ adwuma no ma adesuafoɔ kwan ma wɔnsa tumi ka nsɛm aberɛ biara.
eng_text: The use of the Internet and the World Wide Web allows learners to have access to information at all times.

text: Adesuafoɔ nso betumi de wɔn nsɛmmisa ama akyerɛkyerɛfoɔ aberɛ biara wɔ da no mu na wɔbetumi ahwɛ kwan sɛ wɔbenya muaeɛ ntɛm, sen sɛ wɔbɛtwɛn akosi da foforɔ a wɔde behyia bio.
eng_text: Students can also submit questions to instructors at any time of day and expect reasonably quick responses, rather than waiting until the next face-to-face meeting.

text: Ɔkwan a wɔfa so sua adeɛ a ɛbaeɛ wɔ ɛnnɛ berɛ yi mu akyi no ma yɛde yɛn ho fi deɛ obiara gye di sɛ ɛyɛ ho. Yenni ɔkwan pa baako a yɛfa so sua adeɛ.
eng_text: The postmodern approach to learning offers the freedom from absolutes. There is no one good way to learn.

text: Nokorɛ ne sɛ, yenni ade baako a ɛsɛ sɛ yɛ sua. Adesua kɔ so wɔ osuahunu a ɛkɔ so wɔ osuani ne nimdeɛ a ɛda n'anim.
eng_text: In fact, there is not one good thing to learn.Learning takes place in the experience between the learner and the knowledge presented.

text: Osuahunu a yɛwɔ wɔ wankasa-yɛ ne nsɛm a yɛde ma, TV so dwumadie a agyina adesua so kyerɛ sa gyinapɛn wei.
eng_text: Our current experience with all the do-it-yourself and information presenting, learning-based television shows illustrates this point.

text: Yɛn mu pii hwɛ TV so dwumedie a ɛma yɛhu sɛdeɛ nnoɔma kɔ so anaa yɛnya osuahunu a yɛremfa yɛn ho nhyɛ mu anaa yɛremfa saa nimdeɛ no nyɛ adwuma.
eng_text: So many of us find ourselves watching a television show that informs us of a process or experience in which we will never participate or apply that knowledge.

text: Yɛrentumi ɛnsiesie hyɛn, ensi nsuti wɔ yɛn dan akiyi, yɛrentu kwan ɛnkɔ Peru nkɔ hwɛ tete nnoɔma a asɛi, anaa yɛbɛ siesie yɛn fiepamfoɔ dan.
eng_text: We will never overhaul a car, build a fountain in our backyard, travel to Peru to examine ancient ruins, or remodel our neighbour's house.

text: Nnaase nkɔ ma nsuo aseɛ fiber optic cable links a ɛkɔ Europe ne broadband satellite no, Greenland man no wɔ so bi na emu nnipa bɛyɛ 93% na wɔwɔ wisae ntotan kɛseɛ no so.
eng_text: Thanks to undersea fiber optic cable links to Europe and broadband satellite, Greenland is well connected with 93% of the population having internet access.

text: Wo ahɔhoɔdan (sɛ wɔ te ahɔhoɔdan nketewa mu anaa wɔn ankasa wɔn fie mu) mu no wɔ betumi anya wifi anaa kɔmputa a ɛwɔ wiase ntontan kɛseɛ no so, na ɛhɔ foɔ nyinaa wɔ wiase ntontan kɛseɛ adan anaa mmeaeɛ bi a wɔwɔ amansan wifi.
eng_text: Your hotel or hosts (if staying in a guesthouse or private home) will likely have wifi or an internet connected PC, and all settlements have an internet cafe or some location with public wifi.

text: Sɛdeɛ yeadi kan ahu no, ɛmfa ho sɛ w’agye asɛmfua "Eskimo" atom wↄ United States no, wↄ Canada no, arcticfoↄ a wↄnnyɛ United Statesfoↄ hu no sɛ ɛyɛ atɛmdidie.
eng_text: As mentioned above, though the word "Eskimo" remains acceptable in the United States, it is considered pejorative by many non-U.S. Arctic peoples, especially in Canada.

text: Ɛmfa ho sɛ wobɛte sɛ "Greenland" ↄmanfoↄ no de asɛmfua no redi dwuma no, ɛsɛ sɛ ahↄhoↄ kwati sɛ wↄbɛbↄ.
eng_text: While you may hear the word used by Greenlandic Natives, its use should be avoided by foreigners.

text: Wↄn a wofi Greenland no frɛ wↄn ho Inuit ne kalaalleg (duduoↄ kabea: Kalaallit) wↄ Canada, na wↄn man mu deɛ, wↄfrɛ wↄn Greenlandfoↄ.
eng_text: The native inhabitants of Greenland call themselves Inuit in Canada and Kalaalleq (plural Kalaallit), a Greenlander, in Greenland.

text: Wɔ Greenland no, wonnim sɛ sɛdeɛ wobedi ahɔhoɔ bɔne anaa wɔbɛdwene ne ho adwene bɔne. Wɔ kuro no mu mpo, "beaeɛ a ɛhɔ nyɛ" nni hɔ.
eng_text: Crime, and ill-will toward foreigners in general, is virtually unknown in Greenland. Even in the towns, there are no "rough areas."

text: Awɔ ne tebea a ɛnyɛ a onii a ɔmmoaboaa ne ho no behyia.
eng_text: Cold weather is perhaps the only real danger the unprepared will face.

text: Sɛ wokɔ Greenland awɔw mmerɛ a (berɛ a worekɔ atifi fam no, na awɔw no mu reyɛ den), ɛho hia sɛ wode ntadeɛ ɛka hye ba.
eng_text: If you visit Greenland during cold seasons (considering that the further north you go, the colder it will be), it is essential to bring warm enough clothing.

text: Kyɛ a wobɛkyɛ wɔ ɔhyew mmere mu no betumi ama wo nna ho aba asɛm na woanya apɔmuden mu haw so.
eng_text: The very long days in the summer can lead to problems getting sufficient sleep and associated health issues.

text: Sɛ ɔhyew mmerɛ ba a, hwɛ wo ho yie wɔ Nordic ntontom ho. Ɛmfa ho sɛ wɔmma yareɛ biara no, wotumi ha adwen paa.
eng_text: During the summer, also watch out for the Nordic mosquitoes. Although they do not transmit any diseases, they can be irritating.

text: Berɛ a wɔkyerɛ sɛ San Francisco sikasɛm gyina nsrahwɛ mmeaeɛ a ɛkyɛn so a ɛwɔ hɔ no so no, onya sika firi mmeaeɛ ahodoɔ pii.
eng_text: While San Francisco's economy is linked to it being a world-class tourist attraction, its economy is diversified.

text: Ne fa a ɛde adwuma ba paa ne wɔn a wɔyɛ ɔfese, aban, sikasɛm, adwadie na nsrahwɛ nnwuma no.
eng_text: The largest employment sectors are professional services, government, finance, trade, and tourism.

text: Da a wɔtaa da no adi wɔ wɔn nnwom, sini, nwoma, ɛne amammerɛ a agye din mu no ama kuro no ne nneɛma a ɛyɛ fɛ wo mu no ama ne din ahyeta wɔ wiase afanan nyinaa.
eng_text: Its frequent portrayal in music, films, literature and popular culture has helped make the city and its landmarks known throughout the world.

text: San Francisco asisi nsrahwɛ mmeaeɛ akɛseɛ a ahɔhogyebea ahodoɔ, adidibea, ɛne nhyiamu asa a ɛho twa.
eng_text: San Francisco has developed a large tourist infrastructure with numerous hotels, restaurants, and top-notch convention facilities.

text: San Francisco yɛ mmeaeɛ a ɛyɛ sene biara wɔ ɔman no mu baako a wobenya a Asiafoɔ nnuane: Koreafoɔ, Thailandfoɔ, Indiafoɔ, ne Japanfoɔ.
eng_text: San Francisco is also one of the best places in the nation for other Asian cuisine: Korean, Thai, Indian, and Japanese.

text: Ɔkwan a wotu kɔ Walt Disney World yɛ akwantuo a ɛho hia pa ara wɔ Amerikafoɔ mmusua beberee mu.
eng_text: Traveling to Walt Disney World represents a major pilgrimage for many American families.

text: Nsrahwɛ a "yɛhwɛ kwan" ne sɛ yɛde wiemhyɛn bɛkɔ Orlando Wiemhyɛn gyinabea, yɛbɛtena bɔɔso mu akɔ Disney ahɔhogyebea a ɛwɔ hɔ ara, yebedi bɛyɛ nnawɔtwe wɔ Disney asase so, na yɛasan aba fie.
eng_text: The "typical" visit involves flying into Orlando International Airport, busing to an on-site Disney hotel, spending about a week without leaving Disney property, and returning home.

text: Nkyerɛkyerɛ mu no gu ahodoɔ, nanso yei ne deɛ nnipa dodoɔ no ara kyerɛ berɛ a wɔka sɛ "wɔrekɔ Disney World no".
eng_text: There are infinite variations possible, but this remains what most people mean when they talk of "going to Disney World".

text: Tekiti beberee a wɔtɔn wɔ intanɛt so denam badwam adetɔn wɛbsaet bi te sɛ eBay anaa Craigslist so no yɛ tekiti a wɔde edi dwuma kakra a wo nso wobetumi de edi dwuma boro da baako akɔ mmeaeɛ ahodoɔ.
eng_text: Many tickets sold online through auction websites such as eBay or Craigslist are partially used multi-day park-hopper tickets.

text: Berɛ a yei yɛ biribi a ɛkɔ so wɔ hɔ paa no, Disney bra saa adeyɔ yi: wɔmfa tekiti a obi de edi dwuma nsan mma obi foforɔ.
eng_text: While this is a very common activity, it is prohibited by Disney: the tickets are non-transferable.

text: Sɛ wobɛpɛ sɛ woda ntomadan mu wↄ' Grand Canyon ɛhyeɛ no akyi a, ɛho behia sɛ wonya tumi krataa a wↄde kↄ nkuro nketewa a ɛwↄ akyiri no bi.
eng_text: Any camping below the rim in Grand Canyon requires a backcountry permit.

text: Tumi krataa a wↄde ma no sua sɛdeɛ ɛbɛbↄ canyon no ho ban, na wo nsa beka tumi krataa yi bosome da edi kan, abosome anan a ansaana saa bosome no ahyɛase.
eng_text: Permits are limited to protect the canyon, and become available on the 1st day of the month, four months prior to the start month.

text: Ne saa nti, ↄpɛpↄn da a edi kan na wobenya tumi krataa a wↄde kↄ nkuro nketewaa ansa na woatumi akↄ hↄ kotonimma bosome mu.
eng_text: Thus, a backcountry permit for any start date in May becomes available on 1 Jan.

text: Beaeɛ a wosi ntomadan da mu a agye din bi te sɛ "Bright Angel Campground "a ɛwↄ "Phantom Ranch" nkyenmu no taa yɛ mã ntɛm da a edi kan a wↄma hokwan sɛ nsrahwɛfoↄ betumi abegye ato hↄ no.
eng_text: Space for the most popular areas, such as the Bright Angel Campground adjacent to Phantom Ranch, generally fill up by the requests received on first date they are opened to reservations.

text: Tumi krataa a ɛwↄ hↄ ma wↄn a wↄba hↄ begye yɛ kakraa bi; nea odi kan ba na ɛnya.
eng_text: There are a limited number permits reserved for walk-in requests available on a first come, first served basis.

text: Sɛ wode kaa bewura Southern Africa yɛ ɔkwan pa a wode behunu sɛdeɛ mantam no fɛ teɛ ne mmeaeɛ ahodoɔ a enni nsrahwɛ kwan ankasa no so.
eng_text: Entering Southern Africa by car is an amazing way to see all the region's beauty as well as to get to places off the normal tourist routes.

text: Sɛ woyɛ wo nhyehyeɛ yiye a, wobetumi de kaa biara ayɛ saa nanso wotu fo sɛ wode 4x4 bedi dwuma na mmeaeɛ bi deɛ 4x4 a n'ase wɔ soro nkoaa na wobetumi de akɔ hɔ.
eng_text: This can be done in a normal car with careful planning but a 4x4 is highly advised and many locations are only accessible with a high wheel base 4x4.

text: Hyɛ no nso berɛ a woreyɛ nhyehyeɛ no sɛ ɛmfa ho sɛ Southern Africa wɔ asomdwoe no, ɛnyɛ aman a etwa ne ho ahyia no nyinaa na ɛte saa.
eng_text: Keep in mind while planning that although Southern Africa is stable not all neighboring countries are.

text: Visa ho ahwehwɛdeɛ ne ɛho ka da nso wɔ ɔman biara mu, na ɔman a wofiri muo no nso nya ɛso nkɛntɛnsoɔ.
eng_text: Visa requirements and costs vary from nation to nation and are affected by the country you come from.

text: Ɔman biara nso wɔ mmara soronko a ɛkyerɛ mpofirim nneɛma a wohia wɔ wo kaa mu.
eng_text: Each country also has unique laws requiring what emergency items need to be in the car.

text: Victoria Falls yɛ kuro a ɛda Zimbabwe atɔeɛ fam, ɛwɔ Livingstone, Zambia hyeɛ no agya na ɛbɛn Botswana.
eng_text: Victoria Falls is a town in the western portion of Zimbabwe, across the border from Livingstone, Zambia, and near Botswana.

text: Kuro no da nsuo a ebu fa soɔ no nkyɛn pɛɛ, na ɛno ne beaeɛ a ɛyɛ fɛ titire a ɛtwetwe nkurɔfoɔ, na saa nsrahwɛbea a agye din yi ma wɔn a wɔn ani gye anigyedeɛ a esaine wɔ mu ho ne bɛhwɛadefoɔ hokwan ma wɔtena hɔ kyɛ.
eng_text: The town lies immediately next to the falls, and they are the major attraction, but this popular tourist destination offers both adventure seekers and sightseers plenty of opportunities for a longer stay.

text: Wɔ osutɔberɛ (Obubuo kosi Ɔbɛnem) mu no, nsuo no dodoɔ kɔ soro na nsuo a ebu fa soɔ gye ntrɛha.
eng_text: In the rainy season (November to March), the water volume will be higher and the Falls will be more dramatic.

text: Ɛyɛ deɛ wo ho bɛfɔ ɔkwan biara so sɛ wobetwa nsamsoɔ no anaasɛ wobɛfa anammɔn kwan a akyiakyia a ɛbɛn nsuo a ebu so no.
eng_text: You are guaranteed to get wet if you cross the bridge or walk along the trails winding near the Falls.

text: Wɔ ɔkwan foforɔ soɔ no, esaine nsuo no dodoɔ a ɛkɔ soro paa nti ɛbɛyɛ den sɛ wobehunu nsuo a ɛrebu fa soɔ no yie—nsuo no bebrebe ntira!
eng_text: On the other hand, it is precisely because the volume of water is so high that your viewing of the actual Falls will be obscured—by all the water!

text: Tutankhamun Nna (KV62). KV62 betumi ayɛ nna a agye din sene biara wɔ subɔn no mu, sɛdeɛ wɔ 1922 Howard Carter hwehwɛ hunuu ɔhene kumaa no ahenfo afunsieɛ a na ɛte sɛ deɛ wɔmfaa nsa nkaaɛ no.
eng_text: Tomb of Tutankhamun (KV62). KV62 may be the most famous of the tombs in the Valley, the scene of Howard Carter's 1922 discovery of the almost intact royal burial of the young king.

text: Sɛ yɛde toto ahenfo a aka no nna no mu dodɔ no ho dea, ɛho nhyɛda nhia sɛ wɔbɛkɔ Tutankhamun nna hɔ nsrahwɛ, esaine sɛ esua koraa na deɛ wɔde asiesie mu no nnɔɔso nti.
eng_text: Compared to most of the other royal tombs, however, the tomb of Tutankhamun is barely worth visiting, being much smaller and with limited decoration.

text: Obi biara a ɔbɛpɛ sɛ ohunu sɛdeɛ afunu a wɔakora so no asɛe akoduru berɛ a wɔbɔɔ mmɔden sɛ wobeyi afiri afunu adaka no mu no abam bebu efiri sɛ ne ti ne n'abatire nkoa ara na obehunu.
eng_text: Anyone interested in seeing evidence of the damage to the mummy done during attempts to remove it from the coffin will be disappointed as only the head and shoulders are visible.

text: Sika a na wɔde ahyehyɛ nna no nni hɔ bio, na wɔde ne nyinaa kɔ Egyptfoɔ Akoradebea a ɛwɔ Cairo.
eng_text: The fabulous riches of the tomb are no longer in it, but have been removed to the Egyptian Museum in Cairo.

text: Ɛbɛyɛ papa sɛ nsrahwɛfoɔ a wonni mmerɛ no bɛkɔ mmeaeɛ afoforɔ akɔhwɛ hɔ.
eng_text: Visitors with limited time would be best to spend their time elsewhere.

text: Phnom Krom da Siem Reap anaafoɔ atɔeɛ fam 12 km. Wosii saa asɔredan a ɛwɔ koko no so wɔ afeha a ɛtɔ so 9 mu, berɛ a na Ɔhene Yasovarman di adeɛ no.
eng_text: Phnom Krom, 12 km southwest of Siem Reap. This hilltop temple was built at the end of the 9th century, during the reign of King Yasovarman.

text: Beaeɛ a asɔredan no wɔ no kusuuyɛ ɛne sɛdeɛ wohu no hɔ berɛ a wohwɛ hɔ firi Tonle Sap ɔtadeɛ no ma kokoɔ no foro yɛ deɛ mfasoɔ wɔ so.
eng_text: The gloomy atmosphere of the temple and the view over the Tonle Sap lake make the climb to the hill worthwhile.

text: Sɛ wokɔsra beaeɛ hɔ a, wobetumi de kodoɔ nso atu kwan akɔ beaeɛ a ɔtadeɛ no wɔ.
eng_text: A visit to the site can be conveniently combined with a boat trip to the lake.

text: Wohia Angkor Pass na woatumi awura asɔredan no mu. Eno nti ɛnsɛ sɛ wo werɛ firi sɛ wobɛfa wo paspɔt berɛ a worekɔ Tonle Sap.
eng_text: The Angkor Pass is needed to enter the temple so do not forget to bring your passport along when heading to Tonle Sap.

text: Yerusalem yɛ Israel kuropɔn ne kuro a ɛso paa, ɛmfa ho sɛ aman afoforɔ ne Amanaman Nkabom no nnye ntom sɛ ɛhɔ yɛ Israel kuropɔn.
eng_text: Jerusalem is the capital and largest city of Israel, though most other countries and the United Nations do not recognize it as Israel's capital.

text: Tete kuro a ɛwɔ Yudafoɔ nkokoɔ no mu no abakɔsɛm a ɛyɛ anika no edi mfeɛ mpempem pii.
eng_text: The ancient city in the Judean Hills has a fascinating history spanning thousands of years.

text: Kurow no yɛ kronkron ma ɔsom ahodoɔ mmieɛnsa a wɔgye di sɛ Onyankopɔn yɛ baako - Yudasom, Kristosom, ne Kramosom. Na ɛha abɛyɛ honhom, ɔsom, ne amammerɛ beaeɛ ama wɔn.
eng_text: The city is holy to the three monotheistic religions - Judaism, Christianity and Islam, and serves as a spiritual, religious, and cultural center.

text: Esaine hia a kuro no ho hia wɔ ɔsom adeyɔ mu ne ne titire no mmeaeɛ a ɛwɔ Old City mpɔtam hɔ no nti, Yerusalem yɛ beaeɛ a nsrahwɛfoɔ kɔ paa wɔ Israel.
eng_text: Due to the religious significance of the city, and in particular the many sites of the Old City area, Jerusalem is one of the main tourist destinations in Israel.

text: Yerusalem wɔ abakɔsɛm, fam tutu ne amammerɛ mmeaeɛ, na wɔsan wɔ sotɔɔ akɛseɛ, annoneɛtɔnbea, ne adidibea a nkorɔfoɔ ayɛ mu ma na ahokeka ne anigyeɛ wo mu wɔ hɔ.
eng_text: Jerusalem has many historic, archeological and cultural sites, along with vibrant and crowded shopping centers, cafés, and restaurants.

text: Ecuador hwehwɛ sɛ Cuba manfoɔ no nya nsatoɔ krataa ansa na woafa amanaman wiemhyɛnbea anaa ɛhyeɛ ahodoɔ so ewura Ecuador.
eng_text: Ecuador requires that Cuban citizens receive an invitation letter prior to entering Ecuador through international airports or frontier admission points.

text: Ɛsɛ sɛ Ecuador Suafoɔ a ɔhwɛ Amannɔne Nsɛm so no de ne nsa hyɛ saa krataa yi ase.
eng_text: This letter must be legalized by the Ecuadorian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and comply with certain requirements.

text: Woayɛ saa ahwehwɛdeɛ yi na ama akwantuo ho nhyehyeɛ a ɛda aman mmienu yi ntam no ayɛ deɛ nhyehyeɛ da ho.
eng_text: These requirements are designed to provide an organized migratory flow between both countries.

text: Ɛsɛ sɛ Cuba manfoɔ a wokura US krataa a ɛma wɔn kwan ma wɔtena hɔ no kɔ Ecuadorfoɔ nanmusini no asoeɛ hɔ na woyi no firi saa ahwehwɛdeɛ yi mu.
eng_text: Cuban citizens who are US green card holders should visit an Ecuadorian Consulate to obtain an exemption to this requirement.

text: Ɛsɛ sɛ wo paspɔt no da ne kwan mu na abosome nsia san gu mmerɛ a ɛsɛ sɛ wotena hɔ no akyi. Wohia tekiti a ɛde wo kɔ san ba anaa tekiti a edi mmerɛ dodoɔ a ɛsɛ sɛ wotena hɔ no ho adanseɛ.
eng_text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond your travel dates. A round/onward trip ticket is needed to prove the length of your stay.

text: Nnipakuo nsrahwɛ boɔ yɛ fo, eno nti sɛ ɛyɛ wo nkoaa anaa wo ne adamfo bi no, bɔ mmɔden hyia afoforɔ na monhyehyɛ ekuo a nnipa bɛyɛ anan kosi nsia wo mu na ama ɔbaakofoɔ boɔ ayɛ deɛ ɛwɔ fam.
eng_text: Tours are cheaper for larger groups, so if you're by yourself or with just one friend, try to meet other people and form a group of four to six for a better per-person rate.

text: Nanso, ɛnsɛ sɛ yei ha wo, esaine sɛ mpɛn pii no wɔka nsrahwɛfoɔ no hyɛ kaa mu dodoɔ mu.
eng_text: However, this shouldn't really be off your concern, because often tourists are shuffled around to fill the cars.

text: Ɛte sɛ deɛ wɔde daadaa nkurɔfoɔ ma ɛyɛ wɔn sɛ ɛsɛ sɛ wotua sika pii.
eng_text: It seems actually to be more a way of tricking people into believing they have to pay more.

text: Bepɔ a emu dɔ na ɛware bi wɔ Machu Picchu atifi fam awiei hɔ, mpɛn pii no wobehunu sɛ ɛwɔ amanfo no mfonini akyi.
eng_text: Towering above the north end of Machu Picchu is this steep mountain, often the backdrop to many photos of the ruins.

text: Ɛte sɛ deɛ ɛyɛ den berɛ a wogyina aseɛ no, na emu dɔ na ɛyɛ den sɛ wobɛforo akɔ soro, nanso nnipa a wɔwɔ ahoɔden betumi de sima 45 aforo akɔ soro.
eng_text: It looks a bit daunting from below, and it is a steep and difficult ascent, but most reasonably fit persons should be able to make it in about 45 minutes.

text: Wɔde aboɔ no ayɛ anammɔnkwan no atrapoe no mu dodoɔ no ara, na wɔ beaeɛ a emu dɔ no wɔde dadeɛ ayɛ adeɛ woso mu de foro kɔ soro.
eng_text: Stone steps are laid along most of the path, and in the steeper sections steel cables provide a supporting handrail.

text: Wɔ deɛ yɛaka yi mu no, hwɛ kwan sɛ wobɛhome hyeehyee, na hwɛ wo ho yie wɔ mmeaeɛ a emu dɔ, ne titire no berɛ a woafɔ, esaine sɛ ebetumi ayɛ hu nti.
eng_text: That said, expect to be out of breath, and take care in the steeper portions, especially when wet, as it can become dangerous quickly.

text: Ɔbodan ketewa bi bɛn soro hɔ a ɛsɛ sɛ wofa mu, emu sua kakra na ɛsɛ sɛ wo mia wo ho fa mu.
eng_text: There's a tiny cave near the top that must be passed through, it is quite low and a rather tight squeeze.

text: Sɛ worekɔhwɛ mmeaeɛ ahodoɔ ne mmoa ne mfudeɛ wɔ Galapogos a, ɛbɛyɛ papa sɛ wode kodoɔ, sɛdeɛ Charles Darwin yɛe wɔ 1835 mu no.
eng_text: Seeing the sites and wildlife of the Galapagos is best done by boat, just as Charles Darwin did it in 1835.

text: Po so ahyɛn bɛboro 60 na ɛfa Galapagos nsuo no so - a wotumi fa nnipa dodoɔ firi 8 kosi 100.
eng_text: Over 60 cruise ships ply the Galapagos waters - ranging in size from 8 to 100 passengers.

text: Nnipa dodoɔ no ara di kan kora beaeɛ a wɔbenya no so (esaine sɛ kodoɔ no taa yɛ ma paa wɔ).
eng_text: Most people book their place well in advance (as the boats are usually full during the high season).

text: Hwɛ hunu sɛ onii a wobɛfa ne so akora no yɛ Galapagos nimdefoɔ a ɔwɔ ahyɛn ahodoɔ ho nimdeɛ.
eng_text: Be sure the agent through whom you book is a Galapagos specialist with a good knowledge of a wide variety of ships.

text: Yei bɛma woagyina deɛ w'ani gye ho ne deɛ wompɛ so apaw ɛhyɛn a ɛne no behyia.
eng_text: This will ensure that your particular interests and/or constraints are matched with the ship most suitable to them.

text: Ansa na Spainfoɔ no reba wɔ afeha a ɛtɔ so 16 mu no, na Inca di Chile atifi fam no so berɛ a kuromma a wɔfrɛ wɔn Araucanians (Mapuche) no te Chile mfimfini ne anaafoɔ fam.
eng_text: Before the Spanish arrived in the 16th century, northern Chile was under Inca rule while the indigenous Araucanians (Mapuche) inhabited central and southern Chile.

text: Mapuchefoɔ no yɛ tete Amerikafoɔ kuo a wɔade wɔn ho no mu baako a woanfa wɔn ho anhyɛ wɔn a wɔka Spainfoɔ kasa no tumidie ase kosi berɛ a Chile nyaa fawohodie.
eng_text: The Mapuche were also one of the last independent American indigenous groups, that were not fully absorbed into Spanish-speaking rule until after Chile's independence.

text: Ɛmfa ho sɛ Chile nyaa fawohodie wɔ 1810 (berɛ a Napoleon ko no maa Spain bɛdaa hɔ a na onni aban a edi so bɛyɛ mfeɛ bi no), wɔantumi anye wɔn ho amfiri Spainfoɔ no nsam kosi 1818.
eng_text: Although Chile declared independence in 1810 (amid the Napoleonic wars that left Spain without a functioning central government for a couple of years), decisive victory over the Spanish was not achieved until 1818.

text: Dominican Republic (Spainfoↄ kasa: Republica Dominicana) yɛ Caribeanfo kurow a ɛda hispaniola apuei mantam, na ɛne Haiti na ɛbↄ hyeɛ.
eng_text: The Dominican Republic (Spanish: República Dominicana) is a Caribbean country that occupies the eastern half of the island of Hispaniola, which it shares with Haiti

text: Sɛ yɛde ne mpoano a anwea fitaa aye so ma ne mmepↄw a atwa ho ahyia no to nkyɛn a, ehↄ na wubehu Europe kuro keseɛ a akye yie wↄ Americas hↄ, a afei eka Santo Domingo ho.
eng_text: Besides white sand beaches and mountain landscapes, the country is home to the oldest European city in the Americas, now part of Santo Domingo.

text: Tainofoↄ ne Caribefoↄ na wodii kan bɛtenaa supo no so. Na Caribefoↄ ka Arawakan kasa no, na wↄbaa hↄ wↄ afe 10,000 ansaana yɛn berɛ yi mu.
eng_text: The island was first inhabited by the Taínos and Caribes. The Caribes were an Arawakan-speaking people who had arrived around 10,000 BCE.

text: Wↄ Europe nhwehwɛmufoↄ no mmaeɛ, mfeɛ kakra bi akyiri no, Spainfoↄ a wobedii Tainosfoↄ no so no maa wↄn dodoↄ no so tee koraa.
eng_text: Within a few short years following the arrival of European explorers, the population of Tainos had significantly been reduced by the Spanish conquerors

text: Sɛdeɛ Fray Bartolome de las Casas (Tratado de las Indias) kyerɛ no, efiri afe 1492 kosi 1498 mu no, Spainfoↄ a wobedii wↄn soↄ no kumkum Tainofo bɛyɛ 100,000.
eng_text: Based on Fray Bartolomé de las Casas (Tratado de las Indias) between 1492 and 1498 the Spanish conquerors killed around 100,000 Taínos.

text: Jardin de la Union. Wɔyɛɛ saa beaeɛ yi sɛ asa maa ahotefoɔ fie no wɔ afeha a ɛtɔ so 17, nanso Templo de San Diego pɛ ne dan a aka si hɔ.
eng_text: Jardín de la Unión. This space was built as the atrium for a 17th-century convent, of which the Templo de San Diego is the sole surviving building.

text: Seesei wɔde ɛhɔ ayɛ adwadibea kɛseɛ, na dwumadie kɔ so wɔ hɔ ɛberɛ biara, anɔpa ne anadwo.
eng_text: It now functions as the central plaza, and always has a lot of things going on, day and night.

text: Adidibea ahodoɔ etwa turo no ho ahyia, wɔyɛ kɔnsɛte a wongye hwee awiaberɛ ne anwummerɛ biara firi central gazebo.
eng_text: There are a number of restaurants surrounding the garden, and in the afternoons and evening there free concerts are often given from the central gazebo.

text: Callejon del Beso (Mfeano kwan). Abranaa mmienu a kwan a ɛda ntam yɛ sɛntimita 69 yɛ tete ɔdɔ ho anansesɛm fie.
eng_text: Callejon del Beso (Alley of the Kiss). Two balconies separated by only 69 centimeters is home of an old love legend.

text: Sɛ woma mmofra bi sika ketewa bi a, wɔbɛka anansesɛm yi akyerɛ wo.
eng_text: For a few pennies some children will tell you the story.

text: Bowen Island yɛ da akwantuo anaa nnawɔtwe awieɛ nsrahwɛ a wɔma kayak so akwantuo, hiking, aguadie beaɛ, adidie beaeɛ ne mmeaɛ ahodoɔ pii.
eng_text: Bowen Island is a popular day trip or weekend excursion offering kayaking, hiking, shops, restaurants, and more.

text: Mpɔtam a edi mu yi wɔ Howe Sound wɔ Vancouver nkyɛn, na wotumi kɔ hɔ a wommerɛ denam nsuo so hyɛn ho nhyehyɛe efiri Granville Nsuopɔ so wɔ downtown Vancouver.
eng_text: This authentic community is located in Howe Sound just off Vancouver, and is easily accessed via scheduled water taxis departing Granville Island in downtown Vancouver.

text: Wɔn a wɔn anigye abɔntennim agorɔdie ho no, Sea to Sky corridor ho nanteɛ no hia wɔn paa.
eng_text: For those who enjoy outdoor activities, a trek up the Sea to Sky corridor is essential.

text: Whistler (dɔnhwerew 1.5 hyɛnka afi Vancouver) asetena boɔ yɛ den nanso agye din paa esane 2010 Winter Olympics no enti.
eng_text: Whistler (1.5 hour drive from Vancouver) is expensive but well-known because of the 2010 Winter Olympics.

text: Wɔ awɔbereɛ mu no, fa wo ho hyɛ nsuokyerɛma so agorɔdie a ɛyɛ paa no bi mu wɔ North America, na ahohuruberɛ mu no sɔ bepɔ so sakre twe a ɛyɛ papapaa no bi nso hwɛ.
eng_text: In the winter, enjoy some of the best skiing in North America, and in the summer try some authentic mountain biking.

text: Ɛsɛ sɛ wogye hokwan to hɔ ansa. Ɛsɛ sɛ wonya hokwan no ansa na wobetumi atena Sirena ama adeɛ akye.
eng_text: Permits must be reserved in advance. You must have a permit to stay overnight at Sirena.

text: Sirena nkoaa na ɛyɛ kwaeɛhwɛfoɔ atenaeɛ a ɛma kwan ma nnipa mmienu anaa deɛ ɛboro saa da na wɔma aduane a ɛyɛ hye na abɔnten nsraban mu da ka ho. La Leona, San Pedrillo, ne Los Patos ma abɔnten nsraban mu da a aduane nnka ho.
eng_text: Sirena is the only ranger station that offers dormitory lodging and hot meals in addition to camping. La Leona, San Pedrillo, and Los Patos offer only camping with no food service.

text: Wobetumi agye turo ho kwan tee afi Kwaeɛhwɛfoɔ Atenaeɛ wɔ Puerto Jiménez, nanso wɔngye credit cards
eng_text: It is possible to secure park permits directly from the Ranger Station in Puerto Jiménez, but they do not accept credit cards

text: Turo Adwumayɛbea (MINAE) no mma turo hokwan nto hɔ ma no nntra bosome baako a wɔsusu sɛ obi de bɛba no.
eng_text: The Park Service (MINAE) does not issue park permits more than one month in advance of anticipated arrival.

text: CafeNet El Sol ma kwan ma wo kora beaeɛ no so to hɔ na wɔgye US$30, anaa $10 ma wo twa da-koro; ɛho nsɛm wɔ Corcovado kratafa no so.
eng_text: CafeNet El Sol offers a reservation service for a fee of US$30, or $10 for one-day passes; details on their Corcovado page.

text: Cook nsuopɔ no yɛ nsuopɔ ɔman a ɛne New Zealand bɔ fekuo, ɛwɔ Polynesia, wɔ Anaafoɔfam Pacific Ɛpo no mfinimfini.
eng_text: The Cook Islands are an island country in free association with New Zealand, located in Polynesia, in the middle of the South Pacific Ocean.

text: Ɛyɛ nsuopɔ kuo a ɛwɔ nsuopɔ 15 a apete ɛpo 2.2 million km2 so.
eng_text: It is an archipelago with 15 islands spread out over 2.2 million km2 of ocean.

text: Esane sɛ wɔne Hawaii wɔ berɛ baako mu nti, wɔ tae ferɛ nsuopɔ no "Hawaii down under".
eng_text: With the same time zone as Hawaii, the islands are sometimes thought of as "Hawaii down under".

text: Ɛmfa ho sɛ esua no, ɛkae ahɔhoɔ a wɔn mfe akɔ anim no sɛdeɛ na Hawaii teɛ ansa na ɛdee ne ho ne ahɔhoɔdan akɛseɛ ne mpuntuo ahodoɔ.
eng_text: Though smaller, it reminds some elderly visitors of Hawaii before statehood without all the large tourist hotels and other development.

text: Kuropɔn biara nni Cook nsuopɔ no so na ɛmom nsuopɔ 15 na ɛwɔ so. Deɛ ɛyɛ emu titire yɛ Rarotonga ne Aitutaki.
eng_text: The Cook Islands do not have any cities but are composed of 15 different islands. The main ones are Rarotonga and Aitutaki.

text: Wɔ aman a atu mpɔn nnɛ so, a wɔma ɛmpa a ɛyɛ papa ne anɔpaduane nso no wɔn ama no anya nkɔanim ama abɛyɛ soronko.
eng_text: In developed countries today, providing deluxe bed and breakfasts has been raised to a sort of art-form.

text: Wɔ soro hɔ pɛɛ no, B&Bs si akan wɔ neama titire mmienu ho: ɛmpa ne anɔpaduane.
eng_text: At the top end, B&Bs obviously compete mainly on two main things: bedding and breakfast.

text: Sɛdeɛ ɛteɛ no, ɛwɔ mmeaeɛ a ɛtete saa no ɛsɛ sɛ obi si gyinaeɛ sɛ obenya ɛmpa a ne boɔ yɛ den, ebia mpasotam a wɔde nsa ayɛ anaa tete ɛmpa a ne boɔ yɛ den.
eng_text: Accordingly, at the finest such establishments one is apt to find the most luxurious bedding, maybe a handmade quilt or an antique bed.

text: Nnuane a ɛba berɛ ne berɛ mu wɔ ɔmantam no mu no wɔtumi de yɛ anɔpaduane anaa aduane a ɔhɔhoɔ no pɛ.
eng_text: Breakfast may include seasonal delights of the region or the host's speciality dish.

text: Beaɛ no betumi ayɛ tete ɔdan a agye din a wɔde tete neama asiesie mu, saare a wɔn atwa no kama ne beaɛ a wɔdware nsuo.
eng_text: The setting might be an historic old building with antique furnishings, manicured grounds and a swimming pool.

text: Sɛ wobɛtu w'ankasa wo hyɛn de atu kwan tenten wɔ lɔre kwanso no yɛ adeɛ a ɛho hia obiara esani sɛdeɛ ɛnyɛ kyɛnkyerɛkyɛnn no nti.
eng_text: Getting into your own car and heading off on a long road trip has an intrinsic appeal in its simplicity.

text: Ɛnte sɛ hyɛn akɛseɛ no, wo nim sɛdeɛ woka wo hyɛn no deda na wonim hyɛn no ahoɔden.
eng_text: Unlike larger vehicles, you are probably already familiar with driving your car and know its limitations.

text: Sɛ wosi ntomadan wɔ w'asase so anaa wɔ kuro mu a ɛmfa ho sɛdeɛ ne kɛseɛ te no ɛnyɛ den sɛ ɛbɛ twetwe nkurɔfoɔ adwene aba wo so.
